The holomorphic S-local zeta function has rapid decay uniformly on each closed strip in the positive half-plane.
Twisting a point of the norm-twist chart moves along the chart.
Duality in the norm-twist chart takes the inverse unitary character and reflects the exponent.
Scalar evaluations detect holomorphy of a family of Schwartz--Bruhat distributions, by reflexivity and completeness of the strong dual.
A simple principal part has a pole precisely when its coefficient is nonzero.
A nonnegative real base commutes with conjugating the exponent.
Unitary characters of the complex units that agree on the unit circle have the same angular exponent.

Point evaluation on the Schwartz–Bruhat space is continuous because its absolute value pulls back to a continuous seminorm on every elementary stage. Copied from the private `continuous_schwartzBruhat_eval` in `AppD_SchwartzBruhat/Sec2b.lean`, used here for the point evaluation.

A complex number all of whose powers lie within `r < 1` of one is one. Otherwise the real parts of the geometric sums `∑ n < N, z ^ n` would grow linearly in `N`, while the sums themselves, equal to `(z ^ N - 1) / (z - 1)`, stay bounded.

A continuous character of the units of a nonarchimedean normed field is trivial near one. If `‖t - 1‖ < δ ≤ 1`, every power of `t` also lies within `δ` of one, so all powers of the character value stay near one in `ℂ`, which forces the value to be one.
An extended integer that is at least `-1` and negative is `-1`.
Moving a purely imaginary exponent `t` from the chart parameter into the unitary character: the chart of `χ` at `s` is the chart of another unitary character at `s + t`.
Once the selected places contain the finite different, projection of the restricted global measure is exactly the product of the selected local measures.
An element of a finite completion is the image of an integral unit exactly when its norm is one.
A pointwise null sequence of continuous functionals is uniformly bounded on each weakly compact convex set.
Equicontinuity of the partial projections bounds all individual coordinate projections by a common continuous seminorm.
Sequential completeness of the Mackey dual makes every absolutely summable combination of a pointwise null sequence of functionals continuous.
Gram–Schmidt on the images of the basis admits lifts that retain their own basis coefficient. The residual images have norm at most that of the original images.
Nuclearity gives a continuous denominator seminorm for which the ratios of basis-vector seminorms have uniformly bounded finite sums of squares.
A pointwise null sequence in a sequentially complete Mackey dual lies in an absolutely convex weakly compact set of continuous functionals.
On a barrelled space, pointwise absolute summability under each continuous seminorm gives a continuous seminorm bound on the absolute sums.
The coordinate scalars of a regular basis converge pointwise to zero.
Convergence in the Mackey topology of the dual can be tested by uniform convergence of the evaluations on weakly compact absolutely convex subsets.
Differentiation of a smooth periodic lift multiplies its Fourier coefficient by the corresponding frequency.
A difference of two translated smooth steps partitions unity along each orbit. The extra width of the interval accommodates the transition between adjacent translates.
The net of finite Fourier sums converges in the circle Schwartz topology.
Dominate any continuous seminorm by finitely many of the defining seminorms.
Pull a circle Schwartz function back to its real periodic lift.
The mixed partial in the one-circle case is the ordinary iterated derivative.
Bounding the derivative on a fundamental interval bounds the Schwartz seminorm.
Two extra derivatives give an inverse-square bound for every nonzero Fourier mode.
An integer sequence that is zero up to `A` and one from `A + n` on has consecutive differences summing to one: the finite telescoping sum is all that is left.

The differences of the smooth step `smoothTransition` along integer translates form a partition of unity: for every `u`, the sum over `k : ℤ` of `smoothTransition (u + k + 1) - smoothTransition (u + k)` is one.
Pullback along the quotient isomorphism, scaled to undo Haar normalization.
A smooth periodic lift gives an elementary Schwartz function on the circle.
Restrict a sequence to an injective subsequence that controls the original weight.
Synthesis from polynomially growing vectors with rapidly decreasing, separating coordinates.
Forgetting the exponential weights is the continuous projection to the zero twist.
Multiply a rescaled periodic lift by a fixed compactly supported window.
One constant bounds all the finite sums of squared coordinate norms. It records the total mass of the kernel and the change of Haar normalization.
Use the section as a coordinate and invert the kernel variable to match the fiber integral.
Lift each prescribed coefficient along the section and multiply by its character. The lifts are orthogonal, have a common squared-norm scale, and have the expected character integrals.
The Hilbert-space integral of weighted translates agrees almost everywhere with the scalar fiber integral.
Almost-everywhere equality on the group pulls back to almost-everywhere equality on almost every section fiber.
Left translation by the kernel variable preserves square integrability on the product.
Applying the average after an action multiplies the average by the character.
On the isotype the average acts by the total mass of the group.
Testing the average against a continuous functional gives its scalar integral.
Translating a twisted orbit integral multiplies it by the character.
In a barrelled nuclear space the partial sums of a Schauder basis are equicontinuous by Banach–Steinhaus, and the nuclear basis criterion gives absoluteness.
A lattice monomial grows polynomially on an affine integral line.
Transport the coordinate expansions from the discrete Fourier side. The factor in the transform of a character cancels the reciprocal in its coefficient.
Evaluation of the unnormalized compact average is a continuous functional on the decay space. Evaluate one real twist after applying the compact projector.
The scalar Mellin transform of the character-twisted profile is the group Mellin integral, and conjugating the inverse twist translates the spectral variable.
Contract the split decay tensor with the compact character integral. A pure tensor with normalized conjugate character in its first factor splits this contraction.
Conjugating the inverse profile shift by the scalar transform undoes the forward shift on transformed profiles.
Counting measure on the infinite cyclic subgroup turns its coset integral into the orbit sum.
In one compact character component, successive integer frequencies differ by powers of a single quotient character.
On a discrete group the trivial subgroup is good, since the dual is compact.
All truncations of a discrete Schwartz–Bruhat function belong to one compact set.
In a discrete Bruhat space, pointwise truncation along any enumeration converges in the Bruhat topology, by compactness of the family and continuity of evaluation.
The point mass in a discrete elementary chart has, for each defining seminorm, a bound given by the corresponding monomial at its lattice coordinate.
Domination in absolute value on a discrete elementary stage controls every defining seminorm, since all its weights are lattice monomials.
Every affine cyclic family of point masses on a discrete group is contained in a single elementary stage, with polynomial growth for each continuous seminorm.
A discrete elementary group has no Euclidean or torus coordinates.
On a stage with trivial kernel an arbitrary subset cuts out an elementary stage function, with the same bounds as the original one.
Reflexivity identifies the coordinates of the dual basis with evaluation.
A continuous seminorm of a family of elementary functions is bounded polynomially if the defining seminorms each have such a bound.
A split average and a compatible pair of transforms induce the diagram on the kernel quotient.
Contracting a completed tensor product by a normalized functional is a split surjection. A vector where the functional takes value one gives a continuous section.
Take one polynomial bound for a finite family of weights.
The Fourier transform of a compact group character is the point mass at that character, with height equal to the Haar mass of the group.
A polynomially bounded scalar sequence multiplies every Schwartz sequence on the infinite cyclic group. The weight of order j is controlled by that of order j + d.
A two-sided decay function is dominated by the module and by its inverse.
The homogeneous periodization at the class of a point is the sum of the compact averages over the orbit of that point.
The series of the compact averages over an orbit is summable.
The periodization at the class of a point is the orbit sum at that point.
The orbit series of a two-sided decay function is summable.
The module of a point of the orbit of the generator.
A logarithmic profile is determined by its values on positive-real units.
Express the scalar Mellin transform using the exponential pushforward of Lebesgue measure, with the same positive-real Haar measure as in the split group integral.
Multiplying a scalar profile by a unitary character of the positive reals is a continuous linear automorphism. The inverse multiplies by the inverse character.
A function in the Schwartz–Bruhat submodule is bounded.
A linear functional on the Schwartz–Bruhat space that is bounded by a multiple of the supremum norm is continuous, because the supremum norm is a continuous seminorm on every elementary stage.
A two-sided sequence with geometric decay in both directions is summable.
Unitary modulation is translation of the Fourier transform on the dual group.
In the elementary one-torus all factors except the circle are trivial.
Transport to the circle takes quotient Haar measure to its mass times probability Haar.

Test a transported function against an elementary circle function on representatives.
Realize the tail in a single elementary stage containing the translating element.
Local uniform summability of all jets gives a smooth sum with termwise jets.
The two tails agree up to sign. Each supplies rapid decay in one half-space.
Bound the full multilinear derivative on the cover by the weighted coordinate partials.
On an elementary group, polynomial growth of translated seminorms gives convergence of geometrically weighted translates in the Schwartz space.
Enlarge the elementary stage to contain the translating element, so that every term and the sum are realized on that same stage.
Use the forward tail at positive exponents and the backward tail at negative exponents. Interpolation between two nonzero exponents covers zero.

Mixed partial derivatives of a translate are translates of the mixed partial derivatives.
A contracting twist turns a one-sided orbit sum into a geometric sum of Schwartz–Bruhat translates.
Translating a polynomial weight along an arithmetic progression costs at most a polynomial in the index.

An abstract form of `mem_modulatedCompactSupportSubmodule_iff`: in a function space with generating seminorms, membership in a submodule `Tf` that cuts out compact support, intersected with the kernels of evaluation off a closed set `Z`, means compact support with topological support in `Z`. Stated abstractly so that elaboration does not unfold the decay space.
Idempotence of the compact projection makes each compact integral, hence the whole orbit sum, unchanged by projection.
Write the compact isotype projection in the same (forward translation) convention as homogeneous periodization. In particular its value determines each summand of the orbit sum.
Restrict a quotient equivalence induced by inclusion, using a continuous map into `J` which preserves the supported subspace and acts as the identity on `J` modulo `N`.
Right invariance of Haar measure gives the transformation law of the normalized average.
The projection averages only within a module fiber. Its support stays over the same compact window, whose preimage is compact by properness.
Periodization descends to a continuous linear map from the supported stage to the Schwartz–Bruhat space of `G/(Γ ⊔ k)`: a normalized coset integral over `Γ ⊔ k`.
A closed submodule of a Fréchet space is Fréchet.
The Haar integral over `Γ ⊔ k` of a `k`-invariant function is the measure of `k` times its orbit sum over the generator.
The compact subgroup is open in `Γ ⊔ k`: it is the set of elements whose module has logarithm strictly within one period of zero.
A telescoping smooth profile whose support lies in `[-T, ε]`.
The subgroup generated by the generator and a compact subgroup is closed.
Every Schwartz–Bruhat function on `G/(Γ ⊔ k)` is the periodization of a `k`-invariant function supported in the window: multiply its pullback by a telescoping cutoff of the logarithm of the module.
Transport a primal and dual Schauder basis along a quotient equivalence. Biorthogonality recovers each dual coordinate by evaluating on its primal basis vector.
Inclusion and a continuous choice of supported representative descend to inverse maps.
After twisting by the compact component of the generator, the homogeneous orbit sum is a scalar multiple of the ordinary orbit sum of the compact average profile.
Tensor a scalar profile with the normalized conjugate character of the compact kernel. Compact averaging recovers the profile, and the lift preserves its radial support.
Bruhat differentiability pulls back along the quotient map by a closed subgroup.

The product of a smooth profile of the logarithm of the module with the pullback of a Schwartz–Bruhat function on the cyclic quotient is Bruhat smooth on G. This is the smoothness of u₀ · (φ ∘ π) in the printed proof, for u₀ = ρ ∘ log |·|_G.
A smooth profile of the logarithm of the module is Bruhat smooth.
Compact subgroups lie in the kernel of the logarithm of the module.
A window in the logarithm of the module pulls back to a compact set.
On the positive reals with identity module, if the generator has logarithm one, a lifted logarithmic bump has homogeneous periodization one at the identity class.
A smooth bump of radius 1/2 at the origin sums to one over the integers.
On the positive reals with identity module, a test that vanishes off a closed window whose interior misses the orbit of the identity has homogeneous periodization zero at the identity class.
A test in the decay space of the positive reals that vanishes off a closed window vanishes at every point outside the interior of the window: its support is open.
Left-translated compact profiles tend to zero under the positive singleton weight.
Geometric damping beats polynomial growth of Schwartz translation seminorms.
Test a difference product on a retract. Each single difference has closed image on the retract by pullback, so on a Fréchet retract their product is a closed embedding.
The trivial character takes the value one.
Every unitary character of the positive reals is `t ↦ exp(i s log t)` for a unique `s`.
Through a section of the modulation, a character of the norm-one subgroup extends to a character trivial on the section, and every extension is that one times a character of the section.
Every unitary character of the positive reals is `t ↦ exp(i s log t)` for some real `s`.
An integrand weighted by a function equal to one and a zeroth power integrates to the unweighted integral.
The annihilator of a subgroup is closed in the dual group.
A Schwartz–Bruhat function lies in the norm-one isotype exactly when translating its argument by a norm-one element multiplies its values by the character.
Induction localizes a product of differences. Applying the next expanding difference enlarges a window only in the direction of smaller modules.
A surjection from a closed part of a Fréchet space onto a Hausdorff quotient identifies the target with the quotient by the restricted kernel.
A radial cutoff gives an isotypic representative in a negative window modulo a single expanding difference.
A logarithmic moment along a one-parameter family of characters is the Fourier transform of a single Schwartz function on the logarithmic coordinate.

, applied to Theorem 4.6.1.5, p. 212. The difference quotient is a separable nuclear Frechet space (by `modulatedIsotypicDifferenceProduct_quotient`), and every Schauder basis of a nuclear Frechet space is absolute.

There is a family of vectors of the difference quotient on which the descended log-moments take the values of the Kronecker delta. Interpolating the Mellin derivatives at one frequency while preserving the vanishing orders at all other frequencies gives a representative for each vector.

, via Lemma 4.1.2.4, p. 159. Once the descended log-moments are the coefficient functionals of an absolute Schauder basis of the difference quotient, they form an unconditional Schauder basis of the strong dual, whose coordinates are the evaluations at the basis vectors.

Under every enumeration of the moment family, the biorthogonal vectors are a Schauder basis of the difference quotient with the descended log-moments as coefficient functionals. This is the expansion step: the coordinate series of a quotient representative converges to it because the coefficients decay faster than any power of the lattice frequency. Absoluteness is `modulatedQuotientLogMoment_bases_absolute`.

Translating one test transform gives a quotient vector with moment one at the translated frequency, simultaneously for every admissible order. The section frequency on each cyclic lattice is affine in its integer index.

A continuous seminorm on the Mellin transform space is bounded on translates of a fixed function by a polynomial in the translation. Its degree is the largest weight among the finitely many line seminorms controlling the given seminorm.

Two biorthogonal families of the descended log-moments coincide. Their difference at any index is a class on which every moment vanishes, and the Schauder expansion of `modulatedQuotientLogMoment_bases_quotient` along an enumeration of the moment index (`modulatedPeriodicMomentIndex_enumerable`) shows that such a class is zero.
Parametrize all the moment characters on the Mellin line of one compact isotype.
All indicated jets at a common zero are indexed by the character on its vertical line. Conversely the frequency and the jet order identify that index.
The number of vanishing Mellin multiplier factors is the multiplicity of the corresponding character, including repeated cyclic generators.
Clearing the rational denominators gives one imaginary period for every factor.
Removing some of a finite-order zero within the entire Schwartz–Bergman space preserves the orders at every other point.
The zeros of the finite exponential product have precisely the multiplicities given by the number of its vanishing factors.
A triangular collection in a linear subspace interpolates all the coordinates of one finite jet.
Gaussian damping converts an entire function bounded on closed vertical substrips to an entire Schwartz–Bergman function without changing any vanishing orders.
Pushing Haar measure forward along the modulation introduces one positive scalar, common to all log-moment orders and characters.
Exact order at one zero and the required vanishing at other zeros produce an entire Schwartz–Bergman transform with arbitrary prescribed finite jet at that point.
The Schwartz estimates for the logarithmic line, with the full weight `(1+|x|)^p`, apply to complex derivatives of every fixed order.

A biorthogonal family is determined by its jets on a separating quotient. Representatives at the finitely many base points generate the other vectors by translation, so the lattice sum reconstructs every quotient class.
Log-moment profiles of a decay profile are bounded by every power.
A continuous linear bijection of Fréchet spaces has continuous inverse.
Choose one frequency in a half-open period for each orbit, retaining its jet order. The compact fundamental interval contains only finitely many zeros.

Entire division at zeros of the prescribed orders, followed by periodic strip bounds. The removable-singularity argument uses the meromorphic normal form, as in ForMathlib/Analysis/Complex/BlaschkeFactorization.
In the scalar Mellin chart the restricted difference product acts by a product of elementary exponential factors.
The scalar profile on a splitting determines an isotypic function everywhere.
Pull a scalar profile back along the modulation and twist by the inverse character, placing it in the matching isotype.
For a lifted scalar profile, every moment on the compact-character component is a derivative of the ordinary Mellin transform at the section frequency.
A Schwartz jet sampled on an affine lattice absorbs any polynomial growth of a translated vector and still leaves an inverse square.
Restrict each ordinary Schwartz twist to the section. In logarithmic coordinates these restrictions are exactly the twists defining scalar decay.
Imaginary translation preserves the polynomial bounds on each vertical strip.
A translated cardinal function grows only polynomially in each of the Schwartz seminorms of any line.
On a finite union of lattice orbits, a series of translates weighted by the corresponding jets of a Schwartz–Bergman function converges in that space.
The ordinary cyclic difference at a point subtracts the value at the translate by the generator.
The Fourier lattice gaps can be smaller than the value of the Gaussian at the higher frequency for arbitrarily large positive denominators.
Any prescribed positive one-sided approximation errors occur at arbitrarily large denominators for some real number between one and two.
A pointwise bounded family of scalar-valued continuous linear maps on a quotient of a barrelled space is dominated by a continuous quotient seminorm.
Continuity at zero in the centered norm chart gives continuity at its center.

On a barrelled space, the integral over a compact space against a finite measure of a family of continuous linear functionals is continuous if each test vector gives a continuous function of the parameter. The pointwise supremum of the absolute values of the functionals is then a continuous seminorm, and the integral is bounded by the total mass times this seminorm.
A character on the norm-one group and one on the section determine a unitary character.
Subtracting the real abscissa from a quasi-character makes it unitary.
Fourier uniqueness on the norm section detects a homogeneous function on the entire group.
A vanishing homogeneous theta function has zero integral on the norm section.
Changing the center of the norm coordinate translates its complex argument.

On a barrelled Schwartz–Bruhat space, a functional that is the sum of the values of the test function at countably many points is continuous, by the Banach–Steinhaus theorem applied to the finite partial sums of point evaluations.
Point evaluation is continuous in the Schwartz–Bruhat topology since its norm is bounded on each stage by the zeroth Schwartz seminorm.
Evaluating an inserted test at a shifted idele selects a finite intersection of valuation cutoffs.
Descend a jointly continuous family through open quotient maps on both factors. The stabilizing subgroup acts trivially on the quotient module.
Prescribe a finite set of strict valuation cutoffs outside S.
Cofinal countable chains of finite sets recover the topology of a locally convex limit. It suffices to embed across one new coordinate at a time.
The compact-uniform summable bound allows integration of the theta series term by term.
Finite exclusion followed by dominated convergence leaves exactly the S-units.
Separate continuity for the inductive tensor product descends through the larger quotient.
Recover a quotient-valued operator from its separated scalar evaluations on each tensor slice.
The range of a continuous linear embedding of a Fréchet space into a Hausdorff topological vector space is closed, and Fréchet in the induced topology.
Evaluating a finite combination of Schwartz–Bruhat functions at a point.

Finiteness of the finite S-idele classes modulo S-units and a congruence level: the finite part of every S-idele is that of one of finitely many fixed ideles, up to an S-unit and a factor congruent to one. The norm-one S-idele classes are compact, and the canonical norm section has trivial finite part.
A continuous linear injection between Fréchet spaces with closed range is an embedding, by the open mapping theorem applied onto its range.
A space with a continuous linear closed embedding into a Fréchet space is Fréchet.
A finite power of a Fréchet space is Fréchet.
By the Baire category theorem, the range of a continuous linear map from a Fréchet space lies in one member of a countable cover of the target by closed subspaces.
The indicators of the local integers and of the elements congruent to one modulo a positive power of the maximal ideal are local tests.

Averaging over a congruence level. If the theta function of a test is invariant under the S-ideles with archimedean coordinate `1` and finite coordinates congruent to `1` modulo the `(n+1)`-st power of the maximal ideals, it is a combination of theta functions of pure tensors whose local factors are fixed by the elements congruent to `1`. Write the test as a combination of pure tensors. At each place the dilates of its local factors by these elements form a finite set, and summing over the products of these sets replaces every local factor by its orbit sum, while each summand is a dilate of the test and has the same theta function.
Each S-local theta function is unchanged by the finite ideles close enough to one.
In a discretely valued field, an element congruent to one modulo a positive power of the maximal ideal has valuation one, and multiplying by it preserves this congruence class in both directions.

Templates on the finite coordinates for a congruence level. At each place of `S` take the indicator of the local integers or of the elements congruent to one modulo the `(n+1)`-st power of the maximal ideal. The products of these, dilated by S-ideles and tensored with archimedean tests, span every pure tensor whose local factors are fixed by the elements congruent to one.

Templates for a congruence level of S-local theta functions. There are finitely many functions `β j` on the finite coordinates, fixed by the elements congruent to `1` modulo the `(n+1)`-st power of the maximal ideals, and continuous linear maps `P j c` sending an archimedean test `a` to the test `x ↦ a x₁ * β j (c⁻¹ x₂)`, such that the theta functions of these tests span every theta function invariant under the S-ideles of that level.
A locally constant function with compact support on a discretely valued field is unchanged when its argument is multiplied by an element close enough to one.

Structure of the local tests fixed by the elements congruent to one modulo a positive power of the maximal ideal: such a test is a finite combination of dilates of the indicator of the local integers and of the indicator of that congruence class. Near zero the test is constant, which is a multiple of a dilate of the first indicator. What is left has compact support away from zero, covered by finitely many classes, on each of which the test is constant.

An LF-space exhausted by rising closed ranges of continuous linear injections of Fréchet spaces is strict: the injections form a strict system by the open mapping theorem, so each of them is an embedding.
An LF-space with a rising cover by closed subspaces, each inside the range of a continuous linear map from a Fréchet space, is strict.
An LF-space covered by countably many closed subspaces that are Fréchet in the induced topology is strict. The closure of each defining stage lies in one member of the cover.

Strictness of the quotient of a test space by the kernel of a linear transform into continuous functions, when that quotient is an LF-space. The classes whose transforms take equal values on the pairs of `R n` form a closed subspace. If these subspaces rise to cover the quotient, and each is represented by finitely many continuous families of tests over a fixed Fréchet space, the quotient is a strict LF-space.

Orbit sums at one finite place. The dilates of a finite family of local tests by the elements congruent to one modulo a positive power of the maximal ideal form a finite set of families, and summing a fixed member over this set gives a local test fixed by those elements, which permute the set.
Each S-adelic test function is a finite combination of products of an archimedean test and local tests at the places of `S`.
A Schwartz–Bruhat function in the span of a set is, pointwise, a finite combination of members of the set.
Each S-adelic test function is unchanged when its finite coordinates are multiplied by elements close enough to one.
Dilating all coordinates of a test function by an S-idele translates its S-local theta function by that idele.
Dilating all coordinates of a test function by an S-unit does not change its S-local theta function: the dilation permutes the terms of the series.
The dilation difference vanishes near zero. Its Haar averages are constant on valuation shells and are supported on the finite valuation image of a compact set.
An LF-space covered by countably many closed Fréchet subspaces is strict. The closure of each defining stage lies in a single member of the cover by Baire.
On a fixed coset of the S-units, outside integrality holds everywhere or nowhere. In the first case its sum is the local theta value at the projected idele.
Each continuous seminorm on a Schwartz space admits finite nets on bounded sets.
Evaluate a larger theta class at the old idele and average the difference between two adjacent shells at the new place.
For the inserted integer-ring indicator, only the terms whose new component is a unit survive.
On a pure tensor, the scalar cut is the old theta transform of a finite sum of translates. The operator on old tests is continuous for each fixed new test.
Each occupied valuation fiber is a translate of the old unit group. Take the finite linear combination of the corresponding continuous translation operators.
Global theta is invariant under translation by a principal idele.

The adelic Fourier transform is a continuous linear operator on the global tests. It is linear because it is the Pontryagin-dual transform read through self-duality, and continuous because it maps bounded sets to bounded sets.
A constant whose multiples by `n + 1` converge is zero.
The double adelic Fourier transform has the same theta function. Riemann–Roch twice shows the two theta functions differ by a constant, and both decay at infinity.
The adelic Fourier transform preserves the global theta kernel.
There are idele classes of every norm `n + 1`.
Global theta decays faster than the inverse norm along classes of norm `n + 1`.

A test with vanishing theta function vanishes at zero, and so does its Fourier transform. By Riemann–Roch the Fourier theta is `a / ‖g‖ - b` with `a`, `b` the two values at zero, and theta decays at infinity.
Duality in a norm chart reflects the exponent in one.
The double S-adelic Fourier transform is reflection, and minus one is an `S`-unit, so it has the same theta function.

The S-adelic Fourier transform preserves the S-local theta kernel. At the center of the critical strip the functional equation sends each weighted theta integral of the transform to one of the double transform, which has the original theta function.
Testing a weighted continuous function against all characters recovers the function.
Restriction to a norm-one component is continuous for compact convergence, and restricting a continuation preserves its pole bound.
A continuous function on a compact abelian group whose integrals against all characters vanish is zero.
A quotient by a smaller submodule maps onto the quotient by a larger one, compatibly with the quotient maps.
Descend the component restriction when vanishing on its regular locus characterizes the kernel.
Restrict a bounded-pole continuation and its regular values along the component inclusion.
The principal translation differences lie in the global theta kernel.
On theta classes, norm-one translation therefore passes through the Fourier involution as inverse translation.
An invertible linear intertwiner for an action and the inverse action exchanges the eigenspaces for a character and its inverse.
Norm-one dilations preserve additive Tamagawa measure, so Fourier transform intertwines translation by such an idele with translation by its inverse.
Compose the homogeneous-to-coinvariant identification with the compact average's identification of its kernel quotient with the isotype.
Global theta is unchanged when a test function is translated by a principal idele, since principal ideles are trivial in the idele class group.
Global theta of a translate is global theta evaluated at the inverse-translated class.
A map induced on a quotient by a continuous linear map is continuous.
A Pettis isotypic average multiplies by the Haar mass at any evaluation of a continuous linear map into continuous functions on which the action is the character.
A functional that scales translates of representatives by a character scales the induced action on the quotient by the same character.
S-local theta is invariant under translation by a diagonal S-unit.
The S-unit translation differences lie in the S-local theta kernel.
Multiplication by a norm-one S-idele preserves additive Tamagawa measure.
Extending to a disjoint union multiplies by the integer indicators on its second summand.
Integrating a stage function times one factor at each new place separates over the additive Tamagawa measure, without a pure-tensor hypothesis on the old stage function.
The Fourier integral for an enlarged test function factors into its stage transform and the local transforms of the newly inserted integer indicators.

For a closed submodule `K` and a submodule `V ≤ K`, the closure of `V` in the topology pulled back along the quotient map by `K` is `K`: the image of `V` is `{0}`, which is closed in the quotient, and its preimage is `K`.
S-local theta is unchanged when a test function is translated by a diagonal S-unit, since S-local theta factors through the S-idele quotient.
S-local theta of a translate is S-local theta evaluated at the inverse-translated idele.
A normalized character average splits the inclusion of its isotype. Transposing the splitting realizes the strong dual of any equivalent space inside the ambient strong dual.
A compact set inside an open set is still mapped into that open set by sufficiently small continuous perturbations of the identity.
A neighborhood of the kernel in the ambient group which contains no subgroup larger than the kernel (in fact every subgroup inside it lies in the kernel).
A continuous linear bijection of LF-spaces is a homeomorphism, by the LF open mapping theorem applied to a Fréchet presentation of its source.
In a split norm group, every character with the given norm-one restriction is a norm twist of any one extension.
Units close to one preserve each Bruhat structural subgroup, jointly with their inverses.
Modulo unit translation differences a finite-place test is represented by its finite orbit average. A radial test is a sum of dilated integer-ball indicators.
Point evaluations on the elementary model are continuous for the stage topology.
Every elementary coordinate is realized by evaluation at a representative.

A subgroup of units preserving a structural pair acts on its elementary Schwartz stage. The action realizes inverse-dilation, and each scalar coordinate of each orbit varies continuously with the unit.
A continuous group automorphism preserving a structural pair pulls realized stage functions back by a continuous linear equivalence of the very same stage.
Coordinates in a presentation detect equality after realization.
Left multiplication by a unit is a topological automorphism of the additive group.
Scalar orbit continuity follows directly from continuity of the projected coordinate in the quotient.
Inverse dilation via the unit induces an equivalence by stage pullback.
On a fixed norm-one component, a norm-one translate acts by its character.
An unramified character is trivial on the embedded integer units.
A larger stage adds no new global homogeneous classes at an unramified place. After averaging the new factor over units, each dilated ball is absorbed by a translate of the old test.
Every chart on the global component is unramified outside the same places, and its restriction is a single unitary norm chart on the stage.
The extension from any stage containing the ramified places is surjective on homogeneous classes. Exhaust global tests by finite stages and remove one unramified place at a time.
A stage image in the homogeneous quotient is stable under all idele translations. The canonical archimedean section realizes the norm within the stage.
Weil's insertion formula reflects a vanishing zeta integral at every unramified character in the right half-plane.
Restriction and gluing for meromorphic functions on a disjoint open partition preserved by the charts. The pole bound need not make the regular locus open.
Every norm-one class of `S`-ideles is the projection of an idele that is a unit outside `S` and whose idele class has norm one.
Deleting finitely many places leaves a nonzero Euler multiplier in the half-plane of absolute convergence.
Subtract the value at zero times the integer ball. The remaining radial function has compact support away from zero, meeting only finitely many valuation shells.
A closed quotient of a nuclear strict LF-space has nuclear Fréchet quotient stages.
Extend a representative of a norm-one S-class by one. Its projections to S and T represent classes on which the two descended characters agree.
Every elementary Schwartz–Bruhat stage admits a compatible complete separable metric.
Varying one finite factor of a pure test commutes with the idele translation supported at that place.

On the open stabilizer of a stage the orbit has continuous scalar evaluations. Automatic continuity upgrades this to continuity in the Polish stage topology; barrelledness then gives joint continuity of unit translation.
Vectors with continuous orbit form a submodule. It suffices to check the stage inclusions, and on each stage one may restrict to an open subgroup of units.
Absolute summability of the Euler deviations makes their product nonzero.
Restricting a global norm power gives the corresponding local norm chart.
The two global Weil identities expose the missing local integer-unit mass.
Each local Euler factor is nonzero in the half-plane of convergence.
A finite-support product separates one factor from its complementary product.
A place dividing the different has integer and integer-unit Tamagawa masses strictly smaller than one.
Each local integer-unit mass is a nonzero finite real number.
Removing finitely many Euler factors divides the convergent Hecke Euler product.
The third cyclotomic field has degree two, so some finite place divides its different. This supplies a ramified place without choosing a uniformizer explicitly.
A positive norm chart is a regular value of the local Mellin transform.
Norm powers are unramified at every finite place.
Equal global theta classes have the same value at the additive origin, as read from the residue at the trivial quasi-character.
Equal local theta classes have the same value at the additive origin.
At every finite stage one can prescribe Fourier evaluation at zero to be one.
Global integer-ring insertion preserves evaluation at zero.
Integer-ring insertion scales Fourier evaluation at zero by the product of additive Tamagawa masses of the inserted integer rings.
Integer-ring insertion also preserves the original test value at zero.
The rational adeles are a nontrivial Hausdorff locally compact group.
In the topology induced by a map, a Hausdorff space identifies points with equal images.
The squared-norm Mellin evaluation is nonzero on a normalized Hecke test.
A field whose norm-one Tamagawa mass is strictly less than one disproves raw idempotence.
A nonzero eigenfunctional forbids idempotence when its eigenvalue is neither zero nor one.
The norm-one idele classes of ℚ(ζ₃) have Tamagawa mass π/(3√3) < 1.
Factor the algebraic product through tests. Separate continuity can be checked on a compact rectangle at a time, where one cutoff realizes the factorization.
Compatible compact localizations glue to a continuous operator on all test functions.

The whole group with trivial kernel is the largest structural pair for a real vector group. This stage gives the Schwartz–Bruhat coordinate equivalence. The stage construction follows Ch02_AdelicTheta/Sec2b and AppB_AnalyticNT/Sec4b.
A real elementary factor carries the usual Schwartz topology. The range test is the purely real case of the elementary Schwartz submodule characterization.
Transport the Schwartz–Bruhat kernel along the real vector group presentations.
A continuous linear left inverse on the stage tensors with the identity on the tail.
Split a product on a stage into factors on the selected stage and its complement.
The slice at the tail of an adele is evaluated by varying its stage coordinates. Applying the global principal value before slicing applies the stage principal value to the slice.
Slicing an algebraic tensor against a functional on the tail commutes with any linear operator on the first factor.
The unit of the S-local adele ring that is the given local unit at `v` and `1` at every other place of `S`; translating by it rescales only the `v`-coordinate of the argument.
A continuous functional on coefficientwise formal power series has finite coefficient support.
Shrinking mixed-monomial bumps isolate a coefficient while all lower-order derivatives vanish in norm.
Bounded coefficient polydiscs control every seminorm of the inverse strong-dual map.
a normalized jet basis element can be made small in every lower-order seminorm.
A finite jet and an arbitrarily small tail give a quantitative Borel realization.
a compactly supported mixed monomial and its dilations realize the same jet.
Finite mixed Wirtinger jets can be realized by Schwartz functions, with a linear bound on any prescribed finite family of Schwartz seminorms.
Wirtinger differentiation preserves equality with a monomial near zero.
iterated mixed derivatives of a monomial germ have descending-factorial coefficients.
a mixed monomial germ has exactly one nonzero mixed derivative at zero.
the first Wirtinger derivatives of a mixed monomial.
dilation makes every seminorm below the homogeneous degree arbitrarily small.

For any finite family of Schwartz seminorms, jets vanishing on a sufficiently large finite set of indices admit realizations arbitrarily small in those seminorms. This is the tail part of the two-variable Borel construction.
Commuting Wirtinger powers span every finite word of real directional derivatives.
Take both real coordinates normal in the coordinate-plane decomposition, then use density.
A finite Schwartz seminorm bound gives finite derivative order on each compact support.
The LF topology makes inclusion of smooth compactly supported tests into Schwartz space continuous.
Pure tensors are jointly continuous at zero for the projective topology (copy of the private `continuousAt_projectiveTensor_tmul_zero` of AppC Sec2a_part2).
Differentiating a pure tensor in a normal coordinate differentiates its first factor.
Restricting a purely normal derivative of a pure tensor evaluates its first factor at zero.

A compactly supported distribution has a tempered extension. Cutting a Schwartz test off by a test function that equals one on a neighbourhood of the distribution's support does not change the value of the distribution, and the resulting functional is continuous on the Schwartz space.
Restriction to the coordinate plane commutes with passing a compactly supported test to its Schwartz function: both restrictions are given by inserting zeros in the normal coordinates.
Passing from a compactly supported test on the product to its Schwartz function commutes with coordinate derivatives, at the product type itself.
A smooth bump equal to `1` at `x` and vanishing off the ball of radius `1/2`.
Inserting zeros into the normal coordinates is a continuous linear map of norm at most one whose norm is preserved, hence a closed embedding.
`h ↦ ∑ₖ (∂ᵥᵏ h)(pₖ)` is a continuous functional when `‖pₖ‖ ≥ k` (locally finite sum).
An infinite-order distribution `T = ∑ₙ δ_{(xₙ, 0)} ∘ ∂_{(0,e)}ⁿ` (locally finite, `xₙ → ∞`), and bumps `fₙ` with `fₙ (x_k) = δ_{kn}`: on products `(c • fₙ) ⊗ g` it gives `c * (∂ₑⁿ g) 0`.
`𝓓_K` is not normable: a zero neighbourhood of test functions only controls finitely many derivatives on the unit ball, so some `∂ₑⁿ δ₀` is unbounded on it.
Precomposition with a closed-embedding continuous linear map of norm at most one is a continuous linear map between spaces of test functions.
A test vanishing at zero meets only finitely many valuation shells in its support.
A linear functional commutes with the local principal-value average. On each unit isotype the orbit integral is the integral of a scalar character times a single test.
The unit average of a locally constant compactly supported function, after scaling by a fixed unit, is again locally constant with compact support.
The scalar principal-value formula does not depend on the choice of uniformizer, by left invariance of the multiplicative Haar measure on the integer units.
A left-invariant set integral is unchanged by left translation by an element that preserves the set.
The principal value acts as the local difference on unit-invariant tests and as the identity on the other integer-unit isotypes.
The integer-unit isotypic tests span the local test space: average over the finite quotient of the units by the stabilizer, with its characters.
Every local test is fixed by an open subgroup of the integer units.
Two linear maps agree once they agree on the pure tensors of an inductive tensor product with a projective tensor power.
Weil's local principal value commutes with multiplicative translation, since both only rescale the argument.
The S-local principal value commutes with translation by an S-idele.
Through an inducing linear map into a polynormable space, every continuous seminorm of the source is bounded by a continuous seminorm of the target.
The finite places of a number field form a countable set, since their ideals are finitely generated over the countable ring of integers.
On the product of an old test `f` and a test `g` at one new place `v`, the principal value of the enlarged stage acts through `f`.

An endomorphism of a space exhausted by closed embedded stages is a closed embedding when it restricts to a closed embedding on each stage and commutes with continuous projections onto the stages that fix every earlier stage.

Continuous linear left inverses of the steps of a chain of stages, commuting with operators compatible with the stage maps, assemble into continuous projections onto the stages that fix the earlier stages and commute with the operator on the limit.

At a stage `S` containing the selected places `S₀`, the transition of theta classes to the stage `T = insert v S` with one more finite place `v` has a continuous linear left inverse that commutes with the principal value.
Iterated line derivatives are iterated derivatives along the line.
Line derivatives preserve vanishing on an open set.
Normal-direction-free product rule: differentiating a product in a tangential direction.

Schwartz seminorms of the restrictions to one vertical line on the elementary subgroup `H × ℝ` of the dual. The polynomials and derivatives act in the radial variable, and group seminorms on the finitely generated group supply angular weights.
Tests for which a scalar functional intertwines an operator with a weighted average of translates form a submodule, including integrability in the predicate.
Transport the scalar averaging identity along a linear insertion on a single orbit.
Translation of tests as a linear map.
Inserting a single local test in a fixed pure tensor is linear in that test.
A continuous functional on formal power series vanishes on every series whose coefficients up to some fixed order are zero.
Borel's lemma with uniform bounds: for every bound on the derivatives at zero, one bounded set of Schwartz functions realizes every sequence of Dirac derivatives within that bound.
`y ↦ yⁿ χ(y)` vanishes outside `[-1, 1]` when `χ` does.
The kth Dirac derivative is `(-1)^k` times the kth derivative at zero.
`y ↦ yⁿ χ(y)` is a Schwartz function.
`x ↦ εⁿ G(x / ε)` is a Schwartz function when `G` has compact support.
Pulling back the strong dual of a quotient is an embedding when every bounded set of the quotient is the image of a bounded set.
Every bounded set of the flat quotient is the image of a bounded set of Schwartz functions.
The derivatives at zero of a real power, viewed as a complex function.
The Dirac derivatives of `x ↦ xⁿ χ(x / ε)`, which agrees with `xⁿ` near zero.
For `m < n` and `ε ≤ 1`, every seminorm of order `m` of `x ↦ xⁿ χ(x / ε)` is at most `ε` times a bound that does not depend on `ε`.

A series whose terms are dominated, seminorm by seminorm, by summable real sequences is summable in a complete space whose topology is given by those seminorms, and each seminorm of its sum is at most the sum of the dominating sequence.

A Borel series `∑ bₙ φₙ` whose terms past `m` are dominated by a summable sequence converges in the Schwartz space. Its Dirac derivatives are those of the coefficients, and its seminorms of order at most `m` are bounded by the first `m + 1` terms plus the dominating sum.
The first `N` derivatives of a shrinking cutoff times a function with zero `N`-jet are uniformly of order at most its radius.
Multiplication by a smooth cutoff equal to one near zero preserves the value of a point-supported distribution, by density of compactly supported tests.
Continuity bounds a tempered distribution by finitely many Schwartz seminorms. Localization and the shrinking-cutoff bound therefore make it vanish on a finite jet kernel.
Repeated mean-value bounds on a ball. Each vanishing derivative at the origin contributes one power of its radius.
A compactly supported test away from zero is a finite sum of tests on open sets where the distribution vanishes.

The S-local principal value has trivial kernel: on a selected finite place it is the local principal value of Lemma 5.3.1.3, whose kernel is trivial, and on every other factor of the tensor decomposition it is the identity.

An operator given by the identity on the archimedean factor and by a tensor product of endomorphisms of the finite factors, conjugated by a linear homeomorphism, is injective as soon as those endomorphisms are.
A tensor product of two injective linear maps over a field is injective, by the left inverse of each factor.

The image of the S-local principal value is closed: it is the image of the whole archimedean factor and of the image of the local principal value in each selected finite place, that is, of tests vanishing at the origin there, which is the zero set of a continuous functional.

The S-local principal value induces the topology of the S-local test space: it is the identity on the archimedean factor and a tensor product of endomorphisms of the finite factors, so it is a linear self-map of a space whose topology is transported from that tensor decomposition.
Transport the split injection through the S-adelic tensor presentation.

The S-local principal value is the composition, over the selected places, of its single-place versions: each factor acts in its own coordinate of the tensor decomposition of the S-local test space, so the operators commute and compose to the operator attached to the whole set. The composite is written as a product over a list so that it can be peeled one place at a time.

The single-place principal value at `v` maps the theta kernel into itself: theta of the average of the translates vanishes because theta of every translate is theta of the test at another idele, and theta of the test is zero.
S-local theta of a translate is S-local theta evaluated at the inverse-translated idele.
Finite-place principal values admit algebraic left inverses. On the finite tensor factor these are continuous for the finest locally convex topology.

The single-place operator at `v` is `1` minus the normalized average over the integer units at `v` of the translates by the reciprocal uniformizer times the unit, and S-local theta turns this into the same recipe on the theta function: theta of the principal value at one place is theta of the test minus the normalized average, over the integer units at that place, of theta of its translates. This is the analytic content of (5.3.1.9): the theta sum over the S-units is exchanged with the integral over the compact group of integer units, as in the proof of the formula for the global theta function in one place in `Ch11_ShellStructure.Sec2a`.
The weighted Mellin transforms are bounded in the Bruhat–Schwartz space of the unitary dual on each line of real part greater than one.
Cauchy's estimate on a circle between two neighboring weight lines bounds each radial derivative, uniformly in the angular character and in the test index.
A zeroth-order Schwartz bound extends to a larger angular subgroup by zero. Pointwise comparison transfers that bound with its line constant.
Meromorphic uniqueness extends the functional equation from the strip of convergence.
Cancel the common Tate factor on a punctured vertical line. Continuity of the reflected integrals extends the bound across all exceptional points on that line.
The convergent zeta integral is holomorphic on each positive half-plane chart.

A criterion for bounded θ-classes, after R. Meyer, *On a representation of the idele class group related to primes and zeros of L-functions*, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005), arXiv:math/0311468 (page numbers are those of the preprint). Used: Corollary 4.17, p. 34, with the summation map of §5.2, p. 38; Lemma 4.20, p. 36, at α = 1, with (12) and (15), p. 17, the reflection of weights on p. 25, Proposition 4.4 and (24), pp. 26–28; and the Fourier isomorphism and the bornologies of §4.1, pp. 23–24. The degree-zero isomorphism identifies the S-unit coinvariants, via summation, with `T(C_S)`. A family in the quotient bornology has representatives in one bounded set. With α = 1 the embedding tests this bornology on the weighted lines of real part > 1 for the test and its additive Fourier transform (the involution J reflects the weight as s ↦ 1 − s). We write the Schwartz bornology on those lines on the Fourier side. A norm section splits the dual as a real line times the discrete group of characters trivial on the section. An elementary stage on this dual is supported on a finitely generated subgroup of the discrete factor. On that stage the ordinary Schwartz seminorms are polynomial weights in the discrete variable and derivatives of polynomially weighted functions on the real line. Every group seminorm is bounded by a multiple of word length, itself a group seminorm. The subgroup and the seminorm bounds may depend on the line. Lean proves that bounded classes have bounded Mellin transforms, and the converse when the classes span a finite-dimensional space or are given by even real Schwartz profiles (#7434). The rest of the converse is the classical input `sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_infinite_span_outside_real_profiles`, which is not proved in Lean; what the project added in writing the paper's statement for this library is said there.
In finitely generated abelian groups, finitely many real homomorphisms control all group seminorms; the finite torsion factor costs an additive constant.
The finitely generated angular support detected on one Mellin line fixes every theta class under the norm-one annihilator of that support.
Restricting a section-trivial angular character to the compact norm-one quotient is injective. The resulting discrete dual is second countable.

The forward comparison for all bounded families follows from the zeroth weighted positive-line comparison for individual tests. The same Baire argument works on each actual Fréchet theta stage and for the chosen norm section.
A norm section factors every unitary character into an angular character and an imaginary norm power.
A real lattice coordinate is a logarithmic frequency of a physical norm-one S-local flow for the *specified* norm section.
Polynomial seminorm weights and complex radial powers are controlled by the joint family with one plus the sum of absolute lattice coordinates and the height.
Uniform boundedness upgrades every pointwise bounded family of weighted Mellin evaluations to a simultaneous bound over the family and a bounded set of theta classes.
Bounded representatives of a theta family have one common finite congruence level.
Zeroth-order angular estimates on a line depend only on the restriction to that line.
A finitely generated group of angular characters kills one principal congruence subgroup of the S-local stage.

A countable cover of a Fréchet theta stage by the possible finitely generated angular supports has a nonmeagre member. This one support works for every weight, even if the original single-test estimates use unrelated subgroups.
A common congruence level puts a whole sequence of theta classes in one Fréchet subspace, represented there by a fixed finite family of archimedean Schwartz maps.
A bounded degree-one theta family has finite angular support for every finite set of places: the level subgroup is open in the compact norm-one quotient.
The forward half of Meyer's criterion holds over all number fields of degree one and every finite set of places.

Over a number field of degree one a principal congruence subgroup is open inside the norm-one ideles. If its finite coordinates are near one, they have norm one. At the unique real place, a positive coordinate of absolute value one equals one.
The image of the degree-one congruence subgroup in the norm-one quotient is open. Members lift to actual principal congruence ideles of norm one.
Extend weighted line estimates by zero from a subgroup to a larger subgroup.

At fixed weight a bounded theta family satisfies every polynomially weighted Mellin estimate on each finite angular subgroup. Only the supremum across infinitely many characters requires an estimate beyond the radial strip bounds.

The angular characters trivial on an open subgroup of the compact norm-one group form a finite subgroup. Restriction embeds them in the character group of the finite quotient, since an angular character is already trivial on the section.
Finitely many active angular characters give every zeroth-order weighted estimate on their generated subgroup, even when the characters have infinite order and their generated subgroup is infinite.
One angular Mellin line separates all theta classes. On a finite-dimensional subspace, pointwise boundedness on this line already implies boundedness of the original sequence.

The Fourier classes of a bounded theta family are bounded. On the kernel, the reflected Mellin comparison gives zero on a line, hence on the positive half-plane. This uses the comparison already available in this file.
All tests in a single Fréchet subspace are fixed by one principal congruence level.
The derivative of a raw flow acts by the negative flow exponent on Mellin values, independently of the angular character and the positive line.
On every positive vertical line the integral of the local integer Gaussian against the trivial norm twist has modulus at least half the Tamagawa mass of the local units.
All bounded S-local theta families have finitely generated angular support, for every number field and every choice of the norm section.
For bounded classes, the fixed-conductor comparison only needs the weights across infinite angular support. Finite support has uniform radial strip bounds.
Pullback embeds the annihilator of the image as a closed subgroup of the original annihilator.
The real Schwartz profile criterion covers the rational empty-place stage of the inverse comparison.

decls.classical: R. Meyer, *On a representation of the idele class group related to primes and zeros of L-functions*, Duke Math. J. 127 (2005), arXiv:math/0311468 (page numbers are those of the preprint), Corollary 4.17, p. 34, and Lemma 4.20, p. 36, at α = 1: the direction from bounds on the Mellin transforms to bounded classes, in the cases that Lean does not prove. For a sequence of tests whose θ-classes have one conductor level and lie in one Fréchet subspace of the θ-quotient: if the Mellin transforms of the θ-functions of the tests, and of their additive Fourier transforms, are bounded on every line of real part greater than one (supported on a finitely generated subgroup of the discrete factor of the dual, with every polynomial weight bounded uniformly in the index), then the θ-classes form a bounded set.
decls.deviation: This is what remains of the criterion `sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer`, which is proved from it below. Proved in Lean, and excluded here by hypothesis: the case in which the classes span a finite-dimensional space (`hS`), and the case in which they are given by even real Schwartz profiles (`hreal`; it covers ℚ with no finite place). The other direction of the criterion is proved in Lean as well (`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_general_forward`). The hypotheses `hk`, `hM` and `hm` follow from the bounds and are proved before this statement is applied. The bounds are written without derivatives, which is equivalent (`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_zeroth_iff`), and the conclusion is boundedness in the quotient, which is equivalent to representatives in one bounded set (`sLocalMellinSchwartzBounds_meyer_lift_iff_quotient_bounded`). The paper states its results for bornological spaces and in the variable of the idele classes. Writing them for this library is the project's work and is not proved in Lean: that the bounded sets of the Schwartz–Bruhat space here are the paper's, that the kernel of the S-unit sum is the closed span the paper divides by, the normalizations of the Fourier transform and of the Haar measures, and the seminorms on the dual group. The integrator and an independent reviewer checked these steps against the paper for the whole criterion (#7346); no specialist in the paper's framework has.
