The compactly supported functions with support in a fixed set form a submodule. Consequently, taking the span of their preimages under a linear map preserves the set.
A sequence with all inverse-power bounds defines an elementary Schwartz test on the integer lattice.
The maximal elementary stage of the discrete group ℤ realizes its rapidly decreasing sequences.
Sampling a vertically Schwartz function on an affine lattice preserves rapid decay.
A compact set is contained in a sufficiently large Fourier box.
Each larger-stage quotient representative can be replaced by an inserted test with the same pole constraint.
Tests with compact Fourier support approximate every local test.
The two zero moments can be imposed by subtracting fixed tests whose Fourier transforms are compactly supported.
Fourier inversion gives a continuous inverse on the local test space.

, and the proof of Proposition 7.3.2.2(2)–(3), p. 353. The global Fourier transform of the global insertion of an S-local test vanishes at every adele where the S-local Fourier transform vanishes at the projection, and at every adele having a coordinate outside S beyond a fixed bound. The bounds are at least one and equal to one at all but finitely many places.
An idele whose S-coordinates lie in the S-product region of size `Y` and whose other finite coordinates are bounded by `D` has idelic norm at most `Y` times the product of `D`.

, and Proposition 7.3.2.4(2), p. 356. For any Fourier region inside an S-product region, the global homogeneous theta functions of the inserted zero-moment tests vanish below a uniform positive idelic norm. By Riemann–Roch they are the theta functions of the Fourier transforms at the inverse class, and those vanish above a uniform norm by the product formula.
The S-adelic Fourier transform of a unit translate is a nonnegative multiple of the dilate of the Fourier transform by the same unit.

A level built from a Fourier region that is stable under shrinking by ideles of absolute value at least one at the infinite places and one at the finite places is preserved by the classes of norm at least one. The norm-one part of a class acts by a scalar, and the remaining part is represented by a positive real at one infinite place.
A dilate of a compactly supported function by a self-homeomorphism is compactly supported, and its support stays in a set whose preimage under the homeomorphism it contains.
On the trivial local component the theta kernel has both moments zero, as seen by continuing the class into the global trivial-character residue map.

On each component some principal value attains the full archimedean pole order at every center: its Laurent coefficient of the top admissible order does not vanish there. This follows from `exists_sLocalIdelicZFunction_principalValue_attaining_poles` for one unitary character on the component. Every center of the component is a norm twist of it, the pole multiplicity at a twist is the number of archimedean pole places (the computation in `gammaFiltration_principalValue_bound`), and `mem_sLocalThetaPoleBound_iff_leading` gives the leading coefficient.

The selected centers and orders form a finite index set. Along the norm-twist line of a component each archimedean place has its poles in an arithmetic progression running to the left, and a cutoff keeps finitely many of them.

There is a family of S-ideles indexed by the logarithm of their norm on which every quasi-character is an exponential, and the exponents separate the quasi-characters of one component. This follows from a continuous section of the norm (`sIdeleQuotientNorm_exists_section`), lifted to S-ideles at the points `exp t`: a quasi-character composed with the section is a complex power (`existsUnique_complexPower`), and two quasi-characters of one component which agree on the section agree everywhere, since every class is a norm-one class times a value of the section.

, and Theorem 7.2.1.1(2), p. 334. The Laurent coefficients of the principal value of a translated test are an upper triangular combination of those of the principal value of the test, with powers of the logarithm of the norm of the translating idele. This follows as `sLocalPrincipalPartCoeff_translate` does. By `sLocalIdelicZFunction_principalValue`, applied to the test and to its translate, and `sLocalPrincipalPartCoeff_translate_zeta`, the zeta function of the principal value of the translate is the character value times that of the principal value, off a discrete set of each norm-twist line. Residues only see such germs (`sLocalPrincipalPartCoeff_translate_congr`), and `sLocalPrincipalPartCoeff_translate_laurent` applies with the pole bound of `gammaFiltration_principalValue_bound`.
After the finite principal values, the pole order on a component is bounded by the number of archimedean places with a pole there.
An archimedean place has only finitely many poles to the right of a quasi-character along its norm-twist line.
Every quasi-character with an archimedean pole on the component lies in some cutoff.
Along the norm-twist line through a quasi-character, an archimedean place has its poles at an arithmetic progression running to the left.
The pairs of an archimedean center on the component and an admissible Laurent order form a countable set.
The archimedean Laurent coefficients identify the archimedean polar quotient with the product of complex lines indexed by centers and orders.
Every unitary character of the norm-one group is the restriction of a quasi-character.
There are infinitely many pairs of an archimedean center on the component and an admissible Laurent order.
A surjective continuous linear map from a Fréchet space onto a countable product of complex lines is open.
A class lies in the entire-Mellin subspace exactly when all of its archimedean Laurent coefficients on the component vanish.
A norm twist stays on the component of the quasi-character it twists.
Two quasi-characters on one component differ by a norm twist.
The statement of `sLocalGammaOrbitalQuotient_dual_basis` with its abbreviations expanded.
A continuous linear functional on a product of complex lines vanishes on every vector whose coordinates vanish on some finite set of indices.

On a space identified with a product of complex lines indexed by an enumerated set, the coordinate functionals form a Schauder basis of the strong dual, with evaluation at the dual vectors as coefficient functionals.
On a quotient identified with a product of complex lines through coefficient functionals, the descended coefficients in any enumeration form a Schauder basis of the strong dual.

The strong dual of a space identified with a countably infinite product of complex lines is the direct sum of complex lines over the same index with its finest locally convex topology. The product is identified with formal power series, whose strong dual is the space of polynomials.
The statement of `sLocalGammaOrbitalQuotient_projectiveTopology` with its abbreviations expanded.
Each archimedean Laurent coefficient vanishes on some stage of the filtration.

If a product of lines is identified with a quotient by coefficient functionals, each of which already vanishes on one of a family of larger subspaces, then the maps to the quotients by that family induce the topology of the quotient.
At a new place, the principal value is the difference of the identity and a uniformizer translate on inserted tests. That translate costs exactly one residue size.
The S-adelic Fourier transform of a unit translate is a nonnegative multiple of the dilate of the Fourier transform by the same unit.
Transfer a Fourier-region bound along an idele class. The norm-one part acts by a scalar, so only a representative of the norm in the smaller stage is needed.
A dilate of a compactly supported function by a self-homeomorphism is compactly supported, and its support stays in a set whose preimage under the homeomorphism it contains.

, 349, 360–361. Approximate the truncations of one test's coordinate sequence, or of one unit sequence, by tests whose classes lie in a single bounded subset of the ambient quotient. Product-topology closure asks only for approximation on finitely many coordinates at a time. The bound must be independent of the cutoff, the finite set of coordinates and the accuracy. The periodic comparison on the full fibre above p would supply Fourier interpolants. For polar coordinates one also needs control of the triangular changes at repeated poles across centers. Page 349 applies the change separately at each center. Page 361 invokes the ambient theorem although T may be unsaturated. On a saturated stage only the polar family with a repeated selected pole is left here.
The Fourier jets of an existing theta class decrease rapidly, uniformly over the selected places and the finitely many possible derivative orders.
Restricting the height weight to a translate of a lattice gives the usual rapid sequence space. Two extra powers of the weight give absolute summability.

Assign each indexed jet to one of the cosets that contains it. Extending the assigned data by zero on each coset allows single-order interpolants to be added even when two of the listed cosets coincide.

On the primary fibre every rapidly decreasing array occurs as the factorial-normalized Fourier jets of a theta class. The pole lattices above one rational prime have commensurable steps, so the periodic comparison reduces synthesis to Hermite interpolation on finitely many translates of a common lattice. Only existence of a test is required.

The archimedean Euler product divided by the reflected Euler product and multiplied by epsilon has polynomial relative growth on disks about the primary centers, after removing the archimedean poles there. The reflected argument is on the line of real part one, so none of its finite denominators can be small.
Cauchy's estimate on a disk where the pole has been removed bounds the ratio of Laurent coefficients by the normalized boundary bound times the inverse radius to the offset.
The selected centers lie on the imaginary axis. Only finitely many occur in a bounded disk, since each is a pole of the one meromorphic function on the chart.
A norm section gives one unitary chart for every selected center, with the section exponent as its coordinate.

After canceling the nonpolar finite Euler denominators and removing the central pole, the remaining germ, divided by its value at zero, has polynomial growth on a fixed disk. The canceled factors are normalized to one at zero. The finite factors polar at the center have fixed shape `z / (1 - exp (-log(q_v) * z))`.

Near the selected center the normalized reciprocal of a nonpolar Euler factor is `1 + b * (exp (L*z) - 1)`, where `b = 1 - L_v(c)`. On a disk of radius inversely proportional to a bound for the slopes, their product stays away from zero.
Finite local epsilon factors are continuous, nonzero, and periodic on a fixed unitary chart. This bounds the reciprocal of their product on the imaginary axis.
In a fixed norm chart a finite Euler denominator is a geometric polynomial. The ramified case corresponds to coefficient zero.

Removing a coincident simple Euler pole gives the same analytic factor `z / (1-exp(-z log q))` at every center. Each remaining Euler factor becomes constant after multiplication by its normalized denominator.
The shifted archimedean gamma functions have poles at only finitely many imaginary parts, one for each infinite place.

At a repeated selected pole, bound each lower Laurent coefficient of the correcting factor relative to its leading coefficient by a polynomial in the height of the pole. Only offsets below the multiplicity at the selected prime enter the estimate.

At repeated primary poles, a nonpolar Euler factor over a different rational prime is polynomially bounded in height. For an unramified place this asks for a lower bound on a single nonzero number `|1 - c(π_v)|`, where `π_v` is a uniformizer. At exact coincidence the totalized Euler value is zero, and at a ramified place it is one.

With at most one selected place every offset is zero. More generally, on any family of repeated poles with finitely many distinct centers the local Euler values are bounded independently of the offsets.
Every value of the descended character is a value of the original norm-one character, by insertion of ones outside the local stage.
A selected finite pole is a zero of the totalized Euler factor.

, with the coefficient change on p. 349. At repeated primary centers where the Euler value has norm greater than one, write `z = c(π_v)`. The missing inhomogeneous Diophantine inequality is `1 ≤ C (1 + ‖s‖)^d |1 - z|`. In the section chart, the pole condition at `w` is `b exp(-s log q_w) = 1` and `z = a exp(-s log q_v)`. The two logarithms are incommensurable, the Euler values are unbounded, and no translation of the height coordinate makes both phases roots of unity. For these shifts from infinite-order Hecke characters this is not a known theorem.
If a circle image contains a common positive power of every element, an infinite-order character has torsion kernel.
A quotient by finite units whose circle image contains a common power of every class precludes repeated primary poles when a power of the character descends to an infinite-order character.

Among the shifted phases with a specified primary pole, the homogeneous two-logarithm estimate controls every phase admitting an equally close competitor of at most squared height. The quotient of the phases cancels both shifts.
At a single complex place the archimedean norm-one factor of an integral idèle lies on the unit circle.
Restriction to an unramified stage preserves infinite order, by the finite index of its image.
If the circle image contains a common power of each integral idèle, compactness supplies a common power for every norm-one idèle class.
A power of a character descends through a compact totally disconnected subgroup without losing infinite order.
The integral finite units map continuously into the norm-one group, with the stated image.
A compact totally disconnected group has only finite-order circle characters.
Every repeated primary pole produces a character-trivial norm-one ratio of local uniformizers with nontrivial valuation.
If every member of the character kernel is torsion modulo finite local units, there are no repeated primary poles for this character.

Paper: Theorem 7.3.3.4, p. 360, with the coefficient change on p. 349.
At repeated primary poles of an infinite-order character, keep only strict closest
approaches to one among distinct centers through squared height.
Only infinitely many such centers with unbounded inverse distances remain. A repeated
pole also gives a character-kernel element of infinite order modulo finite units.
No number field of degree at most two has such a pole.
Reconstruction: The paper does not state this. It is what remains of the project's formulation
`sLocalPWOrbital_bases_bounded_interpolation_laurent_other_prime_shift` of the bound that the
change of coefficients on p. 349 needs, after the cases that Lean proves (#7413), and it is not
known whether it is what the author intends.
Gap: For these separated record centers the phases of the Hecke character still need a
polynomial inhomogeneous lower bound (Theorem 7.3.3.4, p. 360, using p. 349).

decls.summary: , with the coefficient change on p. 349. At repeated primary poles of an infinite-order character, keep only strict closest approaches to one among distinct centers through squared height. Only infinitely many such centers with unbounded inverse distances remain. A repeated pole also gives a character-kernel element of infinite order modulo finite units. No number field of degree at most two has such a pole.
Simultaneous periods of two independent integer logarithms have zero height. This separates distinct centers even when their two shifts are non-torsion.
Along a fixed primary pole lattice both unit phases are constant; at the other place the formula holds for the given uniformizer of the statement.
The number of primary primes is at most the field degree, by the ramification-inertia identity.
In degree two a circle image contains a common positive power of every norm-one class modulo finite units. Every primary jet of an infinite-order character therefore has order zero.
A finite idèle with a nontrivial valuation has infinite order in the class group even after quotienting by finite integral units.
With two real places, opposite real exponentials represent the square of an integral idèle modulo finite units.
The diagonal of a global unit is a nonzero period for the real chart.
A nonzero real period gives a continuous circle parametrization of the same range.
An Euler factor of norm greater than one forces the local character to be unramified. It therefore takes the same value on elements of equal norm.
A global unit with nonzero logarithm at a designated infinite place gives a finite-integral representative of the identity class.
The section splits an inserted uniformizer into its norm and a norm-one element. Its character value on the latter is independent of the pole center.

Above one prime all finite Euler factors are rational functions of `X = exp (-s log p)`. A pole of a selected factor constrains `X` to a finite set of roots. In particular the totalized values of every primary Euler factor are bounded on the entire index set.
On the line of real part one, each reflected finite Euler factor has norm at most two.
At large height, the forward gamma ratio is bounded on a neighborhood of the imaginary axis and its reciprocal on the axis costs at most a power of the height.
The leading coefficient of the correcting factor is nonzero. Multiplying the two regular germs in the functional equation gives the leading row of the triangular system.
On the middle line of a Schwartz strip each polynomially weighted norm is bounded.
If every bounded scalar multiplier of a sequence is realized, the lifts of all its truncations are bounded in the quotient. The coordinate equations give the multiplier map a closed graph.

A unit triangular change of a bounded number of jet orders preserves the range of rapidly decreasing sequences if its entries grow polynomially and all rows in a block have the same height. Realize the target in increasing order, correcting one row at a time.

At a selected center, vanishing of the first Fourier jets forces the top Laurent coefficients to vanish. The reflected transform contributes a zero of the indicated multiplicity to the local functional equation.

The selected coordinates separate the ambient quotient. The argument of §7.3.1 for the polar kernel uses the range criterion of §7.2.2, which only needs trivial Picard group at the target stage. The same criterion applies to vanishing Fourier jets.
Compact interpolation of truncated coefficients gives the cardinal vectors and convergence of the ordered sums. Separation identifies every cluster point.
Transport the ordinary expansion back through the level isomorphism. Nuclear Fréchet duality then gives absoluteness and the unconditional strong-dual expansion.

, as used on p. 361. The ambient orbital quotient needs the polynomial seminorm estimate when all places above the chosen prime are present. The base set may be unsaturated at other primes. The lattice is indexed from a contributing pole.

Multiply a vanishing factor by a Gaussian and correct its jet at zero with the Taylor polynomial of its local reciprocal. The resulting cardinal function is Schwartz on every vertical strip and keeps all prescribed zeros with multiplicity D.
Vanishing of the selected Fourier jets cancels the corresponding polar coefficients by the local functional equation, also on a stage which is unsaturated away from the prime.

, as used on p. 361. On one pole lattice and at one derivative order, suppose each point mass has a theta representative. Then every rapidly decreasing sequence has a representative, with all other primary jets zero. Page 346 compares the quotient to a periodic difference quotient for a saturated stage. Page 361 only requires a full fibre at the chosen prime. A comparison with the periodic moment model at its unramified places would suffice.
On a nonempty primary fibre the Fourier jets separate principal-value classes. Use the coefficient criterion of §7.2 at the larger ring of integers.
All residue-field periods above one prime are integral multiples of a common step. Use a common multiple of the (finitely many) residue degrees as the denominator.
Point masses on the integer lattice have exactly polynomial weighted sequence seminorms.
The entire Schwartz–Bergman Mellin model is realized by Fourier transforms of local tests. Only the positive half-plane is needed for the reflected jets.

Hermite interpolation on finitely many cosets of a real lattice, in the reflected Mellin variable. A single sublattice carries the prescribed Schwartz sequence. All derivatives of order less than D away from the selected coordinates vanish.
Rapidly weighted imaginary translates of a Schwartz–Bergman function converge on every vertical strip, with all derivatives. Reflection gives the dual Mellin chart.
A Schwartz function on a vertical strip absorbs arbitrary powers of one plus the norm, including at points near the origin.
The closed graph theorem makes a uniquely determined interpolation operator continuous. We apply the Fréchet closed graph theorem on the graph of the coefficient equations.

A divided exponential vanishes at every nonzero point of the central lattice. The additional factors put zeros on the other cosets while keeping the value at zero nonzero. All these factors are bounded on closed vertical strips.
A character of the norm-one idele classes that is unramified outside `S` is trivial as soon as its descent to a larger stage `T` is trivial, provided the Picard group of the `S`-integers is trivial.
When the Picard group of the `S`-integers is trivial, every idele becomes a unit at all finite places outside `S` after division by a single principal idele.

A finite product of principal values is surjective modulo the union of the absolute levels if each singleton is. The singleton operators preserve that union because each enlarges an absolute level by at most its residue cardinality.

For one inserted pure tensor and one added place, its class modulo the singleton principal value has a zero-moment absolute PW representative at some level depending on the tensor. The lift cited on p. 362 gives no Fourier support condition. Summing archimedean dilates outside a ball removes the Fourier tail modulo the singleton principal value.
Apply the exterior dilation equation in the mixed real and complex coordinates of the infinite adeles.

On the small-stage Fourier side, an archimedean dilation leaves each finite factor unchanged. The archimedean tail equation therefore reduces an arbitrary test modulo a dilation difference to a compactly supported test.
Away from the unit ball, each derivative of an expanding dilate gains any prescribed inverse power of the dilation in the weighted supremum norm.

A compact Fourier correction with the same two moments as the tail solution makes the solution polar. Translating that correction still has compact Fourier support, so the compact remainder is polar as well.
A smooth cutoff vanishing on the unit ball makes the expanding dilation series summable in every Schwartz seminorm.
Summing the dilates outside a ball solves the dilation difference equation there. The cutoff keeps its solution Schwartz at the origin.

Modulo the singleton principal value, translation by the archimedean section of norm q acts on inserted tests by a scalar. Its product with a uniformizer has norm one, so that scalar is the given character value.

Baire's theorem upgrades pointwise finite levels to a common level. The ranges of the addition maps from a closed level times the closed principal-value image cover the Fréchet theta space, so one map has nonmeagre range and is open.
Dirac support supplies a compactly supported test with prescribed value one.

, 355. Insertion of integer-ring indicators multiplies the Fourier value at zero by one nonzero scalar, independent of the test. The scalar is the product of the additive Tamagawa volumes of the inserted rings.
Modulating a nonzero bump by a character can make its integral nonzero without enlarging its support.
Modulo an arbitrary subspace, the kernel of the two moments is still closed: its preimage is the inverse image of a subspace of the moment plane.
An inverse-polynomial lower bound for the nonidentity mixed powers of two fixed bases.

decls.classical: for two multiplicatively independent algebraic numbers on the unit circle, each nonidentity power quotient has an inverse-polynomial distance from one. This is the unit-circle consequence of Baker and Wüstholz, *Logarithmic forms and group varieties*, J. reine angew. Math. 442 (1993), 19–62, applied to the principal logarithms of the two phases and of `-1`. The distance here is the ordinary complex chord length.

decls.summary: It suffices to bound pairs of multiplicatively independent phases on the unit circle.
The nonidentity elements in a positive real cyclic group with generator greater than one stay away from one.
A nontrivial relation between positive real generators places both in a common real cyclic group.
The winding integer disappears upon exponentiating the logarithmic form.
Among the roots of unity of bounded order, the nonidentity roots have positive distance from one.
Only multiplicatively independent positive real pairs and multiplicatively independent unit phases require an arithmetic estimate.
An infinite-order phase is multiplicatively independent of at least one member of an independent pair.
Two bounds for mixed powers, one radial and one angular, control every winding of the original form.
If both projections of the form exponentiate to one, every nonzero form has norm at least π.

decls.classical: the multiplicatively independent, positive-real two-logarithm case of Baker and Wüstholz, *Logarithmic forms and group varieties*, J. reine angew. Math. 442 (1993), 19–62. For two fixed positive algebraic numbers, nonidentity power quotients stay an inverse-polynomial distance from one. Near one the real logarithm is Lipschitz.

decls.summary: Multiplication and division by the complex conjugate give the radial and angular products.
After a fixed power, every mixed product in a dependent pair is a power of one phase. The kernel has a uniform gap.
The two independent algebraic phases already exhibited over seventeen provide a partner for a single phase.
Two finite-order generators take values in a single finite group of roots of unity.

Baker–Wüstholz for three fixed complex logarithms, including the principal logarithm of `-1`. See A. Baker and G. Wüstholz, *Logarithmic forms and group varieties*, J. reine angew. Math. 442 (1993), 19–62, doi:10.1515/crll.1993.442.19, and G. Wüstholz, *One Century of Logarithmic Forms*, §3, pp. 5–6. Proved here from the two classical inputs `LogarithmicForm.positive_independent_power_separation` and `LogarithmicForm.circle_independent_power_separation`, which are its cases of two multiplicatively independent bases, both positive or both on the unit circle (#7513). The constants depend on the fixed numbers. The reduction uses the radial and angular power quotients, and separates multiplicatively dependent pairs on each one-dimensional group.
Removing the common rotation couples the two denominators at distinct heights.
The principal logarithm on the unit circle is bounded by the chord length.
The unit-circle input alone controls the chord of the mixed product.
With no finite places the full principal value is the identity.
Along the chart through the trivial character the archimedean Euler factors are `Γℝ` at real places and `Γℂ / 2` at complex places.
A smooth bump supported in `(4, 9)`.
Every quasi-character of the rational archimedean stage lies on a unitary chart.
A compact set of frequencies fits in a single box. From the compact-box argument in Sec3b.
On the trivial chart the Z-function of a nonnegative bump in norm between two and three has positive derivative at zero.
The translated Fourier theta vanishes if the entire dilated norm fibre misses the support.
A test whose quotients by even powers of the norm are again tests has an entire Z-function on every unitary chart.
Two functions in meromorphic normal form on the plane that agree on the right half-plane agree everywhere.
Evaluation at zero descends to the homogeneous theta space at a stage `T` for an unramified norm-one character, through the insertion into the global homogeneous space.
Every even nonpositive integer shift of the trivial character is a pole at every place.
A finite set of linearly independent functionals separates any one of them from the rest.
Fourier theta evaluation on the trivial component, read from the second Čech coordinate.
A test in the kernel of global homogeneous theta for the trivial character vanishes at zero: after the polar term the homogeneous theta function is small at small norm.
The archimedean additive Tamagawa factors are additive Haar measures.
On the embedded old stage the singleton principal value is the difference with the radial translate. The radial section has trivial finite coordinates.
The multiplicative integral of the norm times a function is c_S times its additive integral.
Rational prime ideals have unbounded residue sizes, even after removing finitely many.
The lower integral of a product of coordinate functions over a product measure on `n` coordinates is the product of the lower integrals.
The lower integral of a product of coordinate functions over a finite product measure is the product of the lower integrals.
The local principal value of a test vanishes at zero.
The pushforward of multiplicative Tamagawa measure to the invertible locus has density c_S divided by the product norm against additive measure restricted to that locus.
A real embedding as a real infinite place.
A normed field with a nonzero element of norm less than one has no isolated zero.
The S-adeles with a zero coordinate form a null set for additive Tamagawa measure.
At the rational archimedean stage the real coordinate of an idele has the idelic norm as its absolute value.
On the trivial norm-one component every quasi-character is a bare norm power.
A finite product of measures with densities is the product measure with the product density.
Over the rationals with no finite places the S-integers have trivial Picard group.
A zero of the entire reciprocal is a pole.
The profiles `ψ(t²) t⁻²ⁿ` are smooth and compactly supported.
Conjugating the identity on a tensor factor by an equivalence gives the identity.
Dilation along the archimedean norm section commutes with integer insertion.
At a real place, the poles along the trivial chart are at even nonpositive integers.
A nonzero value of the entire reciprocal is a regular point.
The residue of `g z / z ^ (1 - n)` at zero vanishes for entire `g` and `1 ≤ n`.
The residue of `g z / z ^ 2` at zero is the derivative of `g` there.
The S-local principal value vanishes at every point whose coordinate at a selected place is zero.
Over the rationals a single finite place is a saturated set.

Over the rationals with S = ∅ and one added prime, the unit levels for every family of cutoff regions miss a class: evaluation at zero is continuous on the theta space, vanishes on every inserted unit test, and is nonzero on some class.
A compact Fourier bump on an open shell can be chosen with nonzero homogeneous Fourier theta at any prescribed idele on that shell.
Two disjoint Fourier shells give a nonzero Fourier theta even after imposing one additional scalar moment. Their common box bound is independent of that moment.
Dividing a test by an even power of the norm shifts its zeta integral.
On a bare norm chart the singleton Euler factor is the reciprocal of the translation-difference multiplier.
The Euler multiplier identifies PV on the trivial singleton-stage quotient with the identity minus translation by any idele of norm 1/N(p).
A real function with a holomorphic extension, growing at least geometrically to the right and bounded below near zero, has positive derivative at zero.
Two is not the square of a rational number.
Every subring of the rationals is a principal ideal ring.
A compactly supported smooth profile of the real coordinate is a test at the rational archimedean stage.
A nonnegative test which is positive at an idele has positive homogeneous theta there.
Every term in the homogeneous theta integral at g has the same idelic norm as g.
The Fourier transform of a translated test is zero wherever its dilated transform is zero. This is the change of Haar measure in the Fourier dilation argument of Sec3b.
Two real embeddings with different absolute values give two real places.
Beyond the product cutoff, the old-stage Fourier theta evaluation vanishes on every representative in the closed unit level, after cancellation of its insertion.
Composing ordinary stage insertion with principal value at the added places gives a closed embedding on the trivial theta component.
The value at zero already vanishes after unit insertion. The remaining moment is one linear constraint on the small-stage test.
The continued zeta function at the norm character is c_S times the additive integral.
Reflection preserves the meromorphic order. The inverse character has no zero at or to the right of the line of absolute convergence.
The entire pole-removed factor is nonzero throughout the closed left half-plane.
Only finitely many adjusted gamma pole centres lie to the right of a given line. The multiplicities are bounded by the number of infinite places.
Linear-algebra core of Remark 7.4.3.3: a block lower-triangular operator on the product of the jet blocks has finite rank exactly when only finitely many blocks carry a nonzero entry.
Applying the operator to the first basis vector of the block at `z` gives the column of entries `d k z` in that block, and zero in the other blocks.
In block coordinates, an operator acting on each block by a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix with entries `d i z` has values zero on the blocks where all those entries vanish.
Absolute convergence on every norm line makes the Mellin multiplier entire.

The archimedean-flat theta image is closed in the zero-moment theta space, because `archNuclearityQuotient_jetEquiv` identifies the quotient by it with a product of copies of `ℂ`, which is Hausdorff, and the quotient map is continuous.
The archimedean-flat theta image is nontrivial: some archimedean-flat test whose archimedean factors have zero additive integral has a nonzero class in the zero-moment theta space.
Smooth compactly supported cut-offs away from the coordinate walls of a mixed real and complex coordinate space that are eventually one at every point off the walls.
Cutting the archimedean factor off near the coordinate walls keeps the zeta integral of some pure tensor nonzero, so a tensor with flat archimedean factor has that property.
If an integrable function has zero integral against every member of a sequence of cut-offs with values in the unit interval that is eventually one at each point, then its integral is zero.
Some pure adelic tensor has a nonzero zeta integral at the square of the norm twist.
A norm twist of a unitary character whose exponent has real part greater than one lies in the half-plane of absolute convergence of the zeta integral.
On the half-plane of absolute convergence the zeta integral is linear in the test.
Some adelic test has a nonzero zeta integral at the square of the norm twist.
A test whose homogeneous theta function vanishes has zero zeta integral on the half-plane of absolute convergence, because the zeta integral is the Mellin integral of the theta function.
Left invariance of the idelic Haar measure turns a translate of the test function into the value of the quasi-character at the translating idele.

At one infinite place the gamma factor vanishes, by Mathlib's convention at the poles of `Γ`, along an arithmetic progression. So the reciprocal gamma product has a zero of positive finite order at infinitely many points.

For a fixed enumeration of the adjusted jets, the descended jets form a Schauder basis of the strong dual of the archimedean quotient, with continuous coefficient functionals on that strong dual. Pullback along the quotient map recovers the original jets. Under the quotient's jet-coordinate equivalence, the basis consists of the coordinate projections. Its coefficient functionals evaluate at the corresponding unit vectors. Each dual vector is already recovered by a finite coordinate truncation.

A continuous linear functional on a product of copies of `ℂ` depends on only finitely many coordinates: the preimage of the unit ball contains a box that is unrestricted outside a finite set of coordinates.

If the quotient by `D` is identified with the product of copies of `ℂ` indexed by `J`, with coordinates the functionals `jet j`, then the closed span of the `jet j` in the strong dual is the annihilator of `D`.
After removing the two poles, the completed generator is nonzero in the closed left half-plane.
The functional equation and the zero-free right boundary exclude completed zeros in the closed left half-plane.
Entire divisibility is equivalent to the corresponding pointwise inequalities of vanishing orders.
The finite and completed regularized generators differ by the reciprocal gamma factor and one linear factor.
A maximum of vanishing orders identifies an entire divisibility condition with an ideal and additional jets.
Separated zero sets in the two half-planes turn the generator product into a maximum of vanishing orders.
The finite generator has the completed vanishing orders together with the adjusted archimedean multiplicities.
Flatness along all coordinate walls makes the archimedean integral entire. Absolute convergence uses the untwisted local estimate, since the character has norm one.
The half-plane factorization of flat tensors is preserved by finite sums, including sums for which only the whole representative satisfies the two global polar conditions.
At a gamma pole the factor regularizing the completed function has order one at the trivial quasi-character and order zero at all other retained sites.
Splitting Haar measure on the ideles gives the same finite factor for every choice of archimedean test paired with a fixed finite test.

Pair the given finite test with a Gaussian at infinity. Its normalized global zeta function is entire. Canceling the Gaussian Mellin factor on the right half-plane therefore gives an entire cofactor of the finite Hecke function for a flat tensor.

A continuous bijection from a quotient of a closed part of a strict LF-space onto a countable product of scalar lines is open. Intersect each Fréchet stage with the closed part to obtain the increasing family of images used by the open mapping theorem.

An entire global transform with the adjusted vanishing orders has a holomorphic finite-principal-value chart. On the left half-plane the completed function has no zeros, and its simple pole on a norm-twist component lowers the required order by one.

On a finite stage containing the ramification, vanishing of the adjusted global jets removes every pole of the local principal-value chart. Replace that chart by a polar-free local test, then undo the finite principal values before insertion.

Every character with the prescribed norm-one restriction belongs to the given norm chart. The two characters agree on the kernel, and their quotient on the section is a complex power. Adapted from the component calculation in §7.2, `sLocalPrincipalValue_chart`.
Adapted from `globalPrincipalValueConverse_mellin_factor` in §6.3. The finite Euler factors in the local and global conventions agree.
Inserting a pure local tensor preserves its archimedean factor. A nonzero value of that factor extracts the inserted finite test by taking an adelic slice.
Adapted from `globalPrincipalValueConverse_mellin_insertion` in §6.3. Insertion through the stage agrees with insertion at the chosen finite place.

Undoing the finite principal values on a polar-free local test leaves its archimedean factors flat. The resulting test still has flat archimedean factors after extension by the integer indicators outside the stage.
Adapted from `globalPrincipalValueConverse_mellin_localFactor` in §6.3. Restriction to the local stage preserves each selected Euler factor.

A flat test with the same Mellin chart as a polar test can be chosen polar. On the trivial isotype their signed polar values agree. On any other isotype a normalized difference of norm-one translates kills both polar values.
At the exceptional point the simple pole of the completed function accounts for the one jet omitted from the archimedean multiplicity.

Removing the finite Euler factors at the stage gives the local principal-value chart. Multiplying it by the finite Hecke continuation and the outside unit masses recovers the global transform of every inserted test.
Unit translates preserve the span of global tensors with flat archimedean factor.
A map to finitely many complex coordinates has a finite nuclear presentation, using the coordinate vectors in the closed unit ball.
Factor a finite-rank map through coordinates on its range and then include the range back into the ambient space.
A nuclear presentation factors through the finite coordinates detected by its equicontinuous functionals.
Apply the sequence-space rank criterion with the uniformity of the given topological additive group.

An equicontinuous family of linear functionals on a sequence space sees only a common finite set of coordinates. Otherwise rescaled tails tend to zero while some member of the family still takes the value one.
Transport the topology generated by all seminorms across a continuous linear equivalence.
Enumerating the adjusted jets identifies the quotient with the space of complex sequences.
A von Neumann bounded set in a space carrying the finest locally convex topology spans a finite-dimensional subspace: otherwise a linear functional unbounded on it would be continuous.
In a Hausdorff space with the finest locally convex topology, an operator with a nuclear presentation has range inside the span of its Banach disc, which is finite-dimensional.
A finite eigendistribution of additive weight extends by tensoring with the archimedean moment. Global rank one then determines it uniquely.
Transport the finest topology of the empty tail without changing the representation of the finite adelic test functions.
The archimedean Schwartz functions with flat coordinate realizations.
Coordinatewise multiplication by units preserves every archimedean wall and hence also the vanishing of every jet along those walls.
Reduction to additive moment factorization and the vanishing of weighted finite coinvariants modulo the restricted flat space and the theta kernel.
In mixed archimedean coordinates the global Fourier value at zero factors as ordinary archimedean volume integration against a fixed finite functional.
A nonvanishing analytic factor times the reciprocal Gamma function at an affine argument vanishes to order at most one.
A biorthogonal coefficient functional picks out the coefficient of its own vector from a finite combination in which that vector occurs exactly once.
The reciprocal of an archimedean Gamma factor is entire, vanishes to order at most one, and vanishes only at `-c - k` for natural `k`.
The reciprocal Gamma function vanishes to order at most one everywhere, by the recursion `1/Γ(s) = s · 1/Γ(s + 1)`.
The reciprocal archimedean gamma factor of `χ` vanishes to order at most the number of infinite places, and only at points `-c v - k` with `k` a natural number.

A Bruhat test supported where the norm exceeds one has Mellin transform bounded by `(r^σ + R^σ) K` on the line of real part `σ`, for some `1 < r` and `1 < R`: the norm is bounded above and below on the compact support.
A test supported where the modulus lies in `[r, R]` has Mellin transform bounded by `(r^σ + R^σ) ∫ ‖φ‖` on the line of real part `σ`.
Poles at `-c v - k` with bounded orders, and transforms bounded by `r^σ + R^σ` with `1 < r ≤ R`, give an absolutely convergent pole sum.
The reciprocal of a finite product of archimedean Gamma factors vanishes to order at most the number of factors, and only at points `-c i - k`.
Continuous functionals on a quotient agree once they agree on representatives.
Summing a function of the center over all jet indices counts each center with its multiplicity, in any enumeration of the indices.

The scalar half of Theorem 7.4.3.2(2): the gamma-pole series converges absolutely, and for every enumeration of the jets the Mellin values at the jet centers sum absolutely to the pole series minus the omitted trivial jet.
On a trivial norm-one isotype the omitted jet sits at a gamma pole, and the norm twist of `χ` there is the trivial quasi-character.
The Fourier characters of a fixed component are norm twists of the chosen unitary character.
A quotient map followed by a closed embedding gives the same closed embedding on the kernel quotient.
An open map onto a closed linear range identifies its kernel quotient with that range.
A continuous endomorphism preserving the range of a topological linear embedding transports to a continuous endomorphism of its source.
Convolving a continuous function with a continuous compactly supported test is continuous.
Mellin multiplication identifies the theta representative of the transported operator with Haar convolution.
For functions of one isotype, it suffices to compare the Fourier transforms on that component.
Continuous integrable functions are determined pointwise by their Fourier transforms.
A Fourier coefficient vanishes when its character does not match the translation isotype.
A map on a quotient has the prescribed graph once it has that graph on representatives.
The convolution identity on representatives gives the graph of the quotient action.
The polar theta Mellin map is a closed embedding on every norm-one component.
Classes modulo a linear kernel agree exactly when the linear images agree.
A compactly supported Bruhat test is continuous, by its zero twist in the decay space.
Multiplicative weights commute with convolution.
The squared norm weight makes a homogeneous theta function integrable on the full class group.
The polar Mellin transform separates homogeneous theta classes by the two global converse theorems, using their respective kernels.
The polar principal-value image has precisely the Mellin transforms divisible by the regularized completed function with the Euler factors removed.
In a multiplication action on jets, the Leibniz terms with a positive-order derivative of the multiplier vanish on the matching biorthogonal vector.
The Schwartz–Bergman divisibility condition is detected by ordinary derivative jets.
Vanishing orders characterize entire divisibility, as in §7.1, `schwartzBergmanDivisible_isClosed_dvd`.

Uniform rescaling of the finite orbital jet expansion. The scaled coordinate vectors must lie in one Banach disc of the polar quotient, while one continuous seminorm bounds the correspondingly rescaled rows of the test action. The residual coefficients must decrease rapidly in a single enumeration (allowing unused indices). The comparison jets in §7.1.4.3 give biorthogonality without these simultaneous bounds. A periodic interpolation estimate in the topology of the polar quotient would supply them.

Polynomial growth of the cardinal Euler jets in each continuous seminorm of the polar quotient. The constants and exponent may depend on the seminorm. A construction of interpolants in the polar Mellin image with polynomial strip bounds suffices, since the jets separate the quotient. This estimate is independent of the test action.
The factor 1 − (1 − H(s)/H(w))ᴺ is a multiple of H and equals one through order N − 1 at w. Multiplication by it preserves all vanishing conditions at other sites.
The jet correction costs only polynomial weights in the centre and the argument. The degree N is fixed for the whole Euler fibre.
Correct translated Euler cardinal functions by the reflected generator before lifting them to the polar image. The uniform bound on the Euler orders fixes one correction degree.

Reflecting the pole - cleared finite generator gives an entire function vanishing to the completed orders. On the imaginary axis its reciprocal has polynomial growth by Theorem B.6.1.6 on the line Re(s) = 1.
The inverse Euler product over one rational prime has common imaginary period 2π/log N(p), since each residue - field logarithm is an integral multiple of log N(p).
One extra power of strip decay dominates the weighted vertical trace by an L² function independent of the jet. A continuous seminorm uses finitely many such traces.
Cardinal functions on one fundamental interval supply cardinal functions on all its translates. The strip weight changes by at most a power of the translation height.
A bounded-order Cauchy estimate with one bound on the entire input strip. The square of the envelope accounts for the multiplier on each integration circle.

Encode a jet by one vanishing local factor, its integer phase and its derivative order. There are finitely many factor/order labels, so the code grows at most linearly in the absolute imaginary part, even when local factors share zeros.

A positive envelope for the test multiplier on the unit circles about the imaginary axis. Its square dominates the multiplier and the envelope itself still decreases faster than every inverse power of the height.
Restricting the Mellin closed embedding to its range and then taking the closed principal-value quotient preserves the Fréchet property.

In a Fréchet space a rapid positive scale absorbs polynomial column growth. Pointwise boundedness of the rows divided by its square gives one continuous seminorm by the barrelled-space uniform boundedness principle.
The Mellin jets up to the full local Euler order separate the polar quotient. The comparison vectors of §7.1 lift to polar classes because all their completed L-function jets vanish.

Synthesize the rank-one series in the complete disc, then use the separating jets to identify its sum with the action. The approximation property identifies the traces of all presentations. Each finite fiber contributes its multiplicity.
The Euler zeros lie on the imaginary axis, where the regularized completed generator has order zero. Thus the two sets of jet conditions are disjoint.
A closed quotient of a space embedded linearly in a nuclear space is nuclear.
A surjective choice of representatives carries a Mellin range equality to a pointwise description on those representatives.
A flat archimedean Schwartz function vanishes at the origin, which meets a wall.
If the additive-mass functional spans the algebraic eigenfunctionals, the weighted translation differences generate its kernel.

Both boundary kernels for the genuine quotient admit entire numerators, uniform reciprocal bounds in unit neighborhoods of their respective integration lines, full retained orders and polynomial derivative growth on every finite vertical strip.
Absolute convergence at two gives a single upper bound on the entire closed right half-plane.
Functional reflection transfers each retained jet to the entire finite generator of the contragredient. The multiplication here is by a nowhere-zero entire epsilon factor.
On the absolute-convergence half-plane the pole-clearing polynomial has modulus at least one. The actual entire finite generator therefore has a uniformly bounded reciprocal there.
In every fixed vertical strip and after any real shift, the derivative of the actual finite generator has at most polynomial growth in absolute height.
Each retained multiplicity is dominated by the analytic order of the entire finite generator at the shifted site used by the actual spectral quotient.
The entire pole-cleared finite generator has a polynomial bound uniformly up and down each fixed strip, including its continued values in the finite-height region.
Gaussian regularization of the Cauchy kernel with its moving pole removed.
The moving, regularized Cauchy vector is holomorphic in its integration parameter where the generator is nonzero, including at the removable diagonal.
The kernel multiplied by a test Mellin transform is uniformly Schwartz in the boundary parameter, including all its derivatives, in each output strip seminorm.

The entire interpolation vector on a vertical contour grows at most polynomially in the contour height, for each fixed output Schwartz–Bergman seminorm. The same bound applies uniformly on any narrow complex tube where the reciprocal bound holds.

Every bounded sequence in a complete Hausdorff locally convex space lies in one Banach disc. The ℓ¹ synthesis construction is from the Chapter 7 biorthogonal certificate; factoring out its kernel removes the biorthogonality assumption.
On two fixed lines a Gaussian-localized Cauchy integral recovers the original Schwartz–Bergman function at every point strictly between the lines.
Every polynomially reweighted fixed-line synthesis has a single rapid presentation after projection to any complete countably-seminormed space.
A separating family of observations has strongly dense span in the dual of a space on which every continuous strong-bidual element is evaluation.
The entire comparison generator gives a globally defined Schwartz-valued kernel. Every polynomially weighted output strip is bounded in the real Schwartz space.

Applying the weighted rapid coordinates of the boundary kernels to arbitrary ℓ² coefficients gives a continuous synthesis into the full Schwartz–Bergman space. The pointwise continuity on the Hilbert side closes its graph.
Polynomial damping of the analysis coordinates realizes an entire Banach family of tempered functionals in one Hilbert boundary space.

Finite interleaving of two rapid presentations over a common source, after precomposition with arbitrary bounded maps. A jointly bounded family of target vectors gives one Banach disc, even when the original presentations used different discs.
A Hilbert-space boundary extension descends through a quotient by first choosing the representative perpendicular to the kernel of the synthesis.
On a neighborhood disjoint from a boundary line, the difference between the regularized and bare Gaussian integrals is bounded by a constant times the generator.
The fixed-line Gaussian integral factors through a Hilbert space. Its output map has rapid nuclear coefficients after composition with the quotient projection.
Restricting to a fixed vertical line gives Hilbert analysis coordinates which reproduce integration against every Schwartz test function.

A smoothing synthesis operator from a separable complex Hilbert space into a complete countably seminormed space has a single rapid nuclear presentation if its orthonormal columns decrease rapidly in every generating seminorm.
A countable family of rapidly decreasing nonnegative rows admits a single positive rapid majorant up to one constant per row.
In a locally bounded family of real-line Schwartz functions, holomorphy of every point value implies holomorphy after application of any tempered functional.
The evaluation functionals at individual real points are dense in the strong dual of the complex real-line Schwartz space.

A family holomorphic on a neighborhood of a whole vertical line with uniform Schwartz bounds for all holomorphic derivatives on that line is a bounded family of real Schwartz functions after restriction.
The weighted boundary kernels form a bounded family in the scalar Schwartz space. The bound covers all their boundary derivatives simultaneously on the same contour.
The signed pair of regularized Gaussian lines has the same finite jet as the original test at each common zero of the indicated order.
A single rapid presentation of boundary synthesis gives a single rapid presentation on the quotient with exactly the same coefficients, vectors, and Banach disc.
Every tempered functional applied to a pointwise holomorphic Schwartz-valued kernel with bounded weighted strip families gives an entire Schwartz–Bergman function.

The two boundary actions descend jointly through the spectral quotient. Coefficients may encode either orientation or the Cauchy normalization. The Hilbert product permits orthogonal elimination of the full synthesis kernel after taking their signed sum.
Locally bounded Schwartz-valued kernels can be tested for weak holomorphy on a separating family. Strong-dual approximation is uniform on the bounded family.
Continuous weighted analysis on a closed Hilbert boundary. The family is linear both in the rapid sequence and in its ℓ² argument, with a single seminorm bound in each weight.
The gamma-stripped, pole-cleared entire spectral generator of the early spectral section.
The entire Schwartz–Bergman space is nuclear through the Fourier–Mellin equivalence.
In the actual retained quotient all nuclear presentations give the same trace.
The compact character integral of an isotype vector is its section value when the compact Haar measure has mass one.
Lift a scalar logarithmic profile by its tensor with the inverse compact character.
The compact average realizes the section profile of the isotype. Its inverse inserts the inverse compact character in the split tensor product.
The unitary phase on the positive reals is an imaginary power.
Shifting the Mellin argument by a real exponent inserts the corresponding norm power in the integrand of a polar homogeneous theta transform.
A fixed first factor defines a continuous map into the completed inductive tensor.
Continuous integrable positive-real profiles are determined by their integrals against the unitary powers.
The remaining operator input is the existence of a rapidly decreasing nuclear presentation of the retained-jet action.
The character-weighted coset integral is smooth on the logarithmic norm line.
By the Leibniz rule, vanishing of the retained jets is invariant under Mellin multiplication. The action therefore descends through both quotients.
The trace terms for the untruncated divisor are absolutely summable throughout the shifted critical strip.

Every finite set of zero sites has a unique continuous projector onto its retained jets. Its range is finite dimensional and invariant under the multiplier, whose restriction has the finite divisor trace.
Removing the gamma factor gives a continuation of the finite L-function. The entire reciprocal gamma factor can only increase the order at a zero.
Disintegrate idèle-class Tamagawa measure over the norm-one classes and the real logarithmic norm.
The test Mellin transform is the ordinary Mellin transform of a compactly supported smooth logarithmic profile.
Every rapid presentation of the retained jet-endomorphism has the predicted divisor trace.
One rapidly decreasing presentation of the descended operator whose scalar series sums to the explicit zero formula.
A Schwartz–Bruhat function on a group identified with the positive real line has a Schwartz profile in logarithmic coordinates.
A summable weighted zero count dominates functions that decay quadratically outside bounded height.
On each bounded vertical strip the Mellin transform of a compactly supported test decays faster than any fixed inverse power of the height.
Zeros in a vertical strip, counted with multiplicity, have a summable quadratic weight.
At a zero of the regularized completed function, its finite analytic multiplicity is exactly the order in the original divisor.
The inclusion of the complete gauge space of a Banach disc into the ambient space is continuous.
Synthesis of an absolutely summable, uniformly seminorm-bounded series into a Banach space.
Any pointwise absolutely converging rank-one expansion on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space gives its algebraic trace by contraction.
Finite supported trace approximations identify the numerical trace of an already rapid presentation, irrespective of whether the cutoff operators are equicontinuous.
Factor a rapid presentation through ℓ² by giving the synthesis vectors the weights `(n + 1)⁻²`. Project away the kernel of synthesis to obtain an injective Hilbert-to-quotient map.
The Hilbert representation of a finite spectral mask computes its algebraic trace without any estimate on the original (possibly very oblique) mask.
Once finite mass-zero factors may be discarded modulo a submodule, the total moment of a flat tensor sum can be imposed on one archimedean representative.
Points of the finite adeles of `ℚ` leaving every compact set at one place: the negative powers of a uniformizer there and one elsewhere.

On a barrelled space identified with an inductive tensor product, the supremum of the seminorms `t ↦ P j (slice of t along ε j)` is a continuous seminorm, as soon as every tensor has only finitely many slices that are not zero.

For points of the finite adeles leaving every compact set at one place, every tensor of adelic factors has only finitely many slices at these points that are not zero: an adelic Schwartz–Bruhat function is a finite sum of archimedean functions times indicators of compact rectangles.

Every neighbourhood of zero in the flat archimedean Schwartz space of `ℚ` contains functions with arbitrarily large weighted supremum of one fixed order: a neighbourhood controls finitely many weights, and spreading a fixed bump out beats the next one.
The indicator of the integral finite adeles is a Schwartz–Bruhat function.
A flat test whose theta class is pole-free for the trivial norm-one character has Fourier value zero at the origin.

Over any number field there is an archimedean-flat adelic tensor whose Fourier value at the origin is nonzero: a nonnegative bump away from the coordinate walls times the indicator of the integral finite adeles.

For the trivial norm-one character, equal homogeneous theta functions force equal Fourier values at the origin, once both tests vanish at the origin and the second Fourier value is zero. The polar term `|x|⁻¹ f̂(0)` blows up at small norm while the theta difference decays.
The indicator of a compact open subgroup is a Schwartz–Bruhat function.
The integral finite adeles form a compact open additive subgroup.
The integral finite adeles are compact.
The integral finite adeles are open.
The norm-one idele classes have positive Tamagawa mass.
The reciprocal gamma factor of `|·|^i` has positive finite order at each `-i - 2n`.
The gamma factor of `|·|^i` vanishes at every point `-i - 2n` of the real pole progression.
The printed jet index set for `|·|^i` over `ℚ` is countably infinite: it lies over the discrete gamma-pole set and contains `(-i - 2n, 0)` for every `n`.
The printed index contains `(-i - 2n, 0)` for every `n`: the norm-character correction never fires on the real pole progression.
The unitary character `|·|^i` of the rational idele class group.
The value of `χ` on an idele class, for `χ = |·|^i`.
The test combination `φ - (3/2) φ(a⁻¹ ·) + (1/2) φ(a⁻² ·)` for the rational idele `a` of norm two.
Residue at `1`: the Fourier value of the combination at zero vanishes.
The reciprocal gamma factor of `|·|^i` has positive finite order at `-i`.
The gamma factor of `|·|^i` vanishes at `-i`.
The multiplier `m w = 1 - (3/2) 2^w + (1/2) 4^w` has derivative `-(log 2)/2` at `0`.
A flat zero-moment polar test whose zeta function at the trivial quasi-character is nonzero.
Away from the two pole characters, the zeta function of the combination is the multiplier `(1 - 2^w)(1 - 2^w/2)` times that of `φ`.
The printed index contains `(-i, 0)` for `|·|^i`.
`|·|^i` is trivial on norm-one classes.
The archimedean parameters of `|·|^i` are `(i, 0)`.
The rational section acts on the real coordinate by multiplication.
Residue at `0`: the combination has a finite limit at the trivial quasi-character.
A bump equal to one near zero, tensored with the indicator of the integral finite adeles.
For any finite factor `g` with `g 0 = 1`, the tensor of a bump equal to one near zero with `g` gives a combination that is a flat zero-moment tensor.
Translating by `a₂` halves the real coordinate and fixes the finite part.
An endomorphism of a quotient module is zero when its graph is described by convolution with the zero function, through a linear transform of representatives.
An endomorphism of a quotient induced by the zero operator is zero.
A real radial test on the rational class group pairs positively with any continuous weight positive on its log-norm window.
The two correction terms differ because only the shifted correction has a nonzero imaginary part.
The rational gamma factor in the norm-power chart is a translate of the trivial one.

A Schwartz function of the mixed archimedean coordinates of `ℚ` that is odd, flat along the coordinate walls and equal to one at the point with all coordinates one: the difference of a bump around that point and its reflection.
An odd `S`-adelic test has zero `S`-local homogeneous theta transform: in its `S`-unit sum the terms of a unit and of its negative cancel.
Over `ℚ` with no finite place, a Schwartz function of the mixed archimedean coordinates is a Schwartz–Bruhat function of the `S`-adele.
On a fixed vertical line, the absolute value of the norm power is independent of height, so dominated convergence gives continuity of the Mellin transform.
The rational gamma logarithmic derivative has order minus one at minus two.

A continuous multiplier nonzero at a simple pole leaves a vertical integrand whose norm dominates a positive multiple of `1 / |t|`. This is the simple-pole argument from `Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec1a_Printed`.
When a submodule surjects onto a quotient, the quotient by its image is zero, so its rank is not two.

The class of the rational idele equal to `-1` at one finite place and `1` elsewhere is not the identity: a principal idele with archimedean component one is one. Copied from the private lemma `strongCoprimality_false_neg_one_ne` of `Sec5_Printed.lean`.
On a quotient of the entire Schwartz–Bergman space a height-square weighted family of point evaluations in a fixed strip is bounded on every bounded set.
A compact rectangle contains only finitely many points of the completed divisor.
Euler nonvanishing and reflection put all positive zeros of the rational completed zeta function in the unit window.
Differentiate a compactly supported radial test in the log-norm coordinate.
Pole removal preserves the multiplicity in the open critical strip.
At any prescribed complex point, cancel its norm power in a smooth radial test. The first Mellin derivative becomes a positive second log moment of a bump.
The reflected zeta function of a Fourier transformed test is analytic at the evaluation point of an imaginary-axis center, away from the exceptional center of the norm twist.
The reflected jet, read on the full homogeneous theta space, is a continuous linear functional taking a test to the corresponding derivative of its reflected zeta function.
A space with a closed linear embedding into a Fréchet space is Fréchet.
Two zero-moment tests with the same homogeneous theta function give the same class, so a map with the theta values separates the classes of the pole-free theta space.

The homogeneous theta functions of zero-moment tests form a closed subspace of the exponentially decaying isotype: the range of any continuous linear map that sends the class of a zero-moment test to its homogeneous theta function is closed. The group Mellin transform of the isotype sends that range onto the pole-free theta Mellin image, which is the (unshifted) spectral nuclearity denominator of Equation (7.4.0.1) in the Schwartz-Bergman model, a closed divisible subspace.

The homogeneous theta functions of zero-moment tests form a closed subspace of the exponentially decaying isotype, so the theta transform is a topological embedding. The paper obtains this from the Mellin model of §7.4, where the theta image is the closed denominator of the nuclearity quotient.
An injective continuous linear map with closed range from a quotient of a closed subspace of a strict LF-space into a Fréchet space is inducing, by the open mapping theorem onto its range.
Closed graph theorem between Fréchet spaces. The proof is the one of the private `weilTest_continuous_of_isClosed_graph` in `AppB_AnalyticNT/Sec4b.lean`, for the whole space.
At a fixed idele class, global homogeneous theta is continuous in the test function.

A linear map from a final locally convex topology to a polynormable space is continuous if its composites with the defining maps are. The proof is the one of the private `continuous_of_locallyConvexFinalTopology` in `AppC_LCTVS/Sec2b.lean`.

On a barrelled space, the integral over a compact space of a family of continuous linear functionals is continuous if each test vector gives a continuous function of the parameter. The proof is the one of the private `continuous_integral_of_continuous_eval` in `Ch05_ThetaZSpaces/Sec1.lean`.

The homogeneous theta function of a zero-moment test decays exponentially in both directions: each real twist is the isotypic average of the corresponding twist of the plain theta function (Remark 9.2.0.1), up to the volume of the norm-one classes.

At a fixed idele class, global theta is continuous in the test function, by the Banach–Steinhaus theorem on the barrelled Schwartz–Bruhat space applied to the finite partial sums of point evaluations. The proof is the one of the private `adelicTheta_eval_continuous` in `Ch05_ThetaZSpaces/Sec1.lean`.
A space whose strong dual is finite-dimensional is finite-dimensional.
Riesz's theorem: a compact set with nonempty interior in a Hausdorff topological vector space forces finite-dimensionality.
A linear equivalence preserves infinite-dimensionality.
An identity between linear maps after the S-local principal value can be checked on pure tensors.
At zero the Fourier transform of a pure tensor factors into the archimedean integral and the product of the finite local integrals.
Dilation by a local unit rescales additive Haar integration.
The local principal value rescales the integral by a scalar independent of the test.
The boundary line of absolute convergence lies in the existing zero-free region.
The strong-coprimality equivalence transfers the nuclear Fréchet structure from its difference quotient.
The comparison denominator is an expanding difference-product range, whose quotient is separable, nuclear, and Fréchet.
A norm-one character extends by projecting along a section of the class norm.
Applying the global principal value to two representatives with equal homogeneous theta class preserves their equality on every norm-one character.
On a nontrivial character, a normalized translate-minus-identity keeps the homogeneous class and kills the two trivial-character residues.
Insertion intertwines the local and global principal values on homogeneous classes. This follows by first passing to ordinary theta and then taking the character average.
Two surjections onto the same finite-dimensional space have equal kernels if one kernel contains the other: the induced endomorphism is surjective and thus injective.
Equality of two polar classes can be checked in the unrestricted homogeneous quotient.
Openness onto the range of a continuous injection detects openness on its domain.
The open quotient on unrestricted tests remains open on the two-moment kernels. The only algebraic input is that polar global classes admit polar S-local representatives.
If insertion induces an open surjection from polar tests onto global polar theta classes, the unrestricted insertion isomorphism identifies the kernel and gives the polar isomorphism.

Every globally polar test has the same homogeneous theta class as an inserted S-local test with vanishing moments. The trivial character detects polar tests by the two residues, and a nontrivial character admits a normalized unit difference.
The global residue map on the trivial component, composed with local insertion, is a continuous surjection to both residues, with kernel the local polar tests.
A bijection carrying a family of generators to the corresponding family transports their spans. It suffices that the global operation respects equality of classes.
A continuous map with finite-dimensional range is strict. Strictness can therefore be exchanged across the two kernels to restrict an open quotient to zero-moment tests.
Translating a local test by an S-integral representative of a norm-one class multiplies its inserted homogeneous theta class by the value of the character.
Each norm-one class has an idelic representative integral and invertible outside S when the S-integer Picard group is trivial.
The inserted unrestricted S-local tests cover a complete unramified theta component when the S-integer Picard group is trivial.
Discard ramified places, synthesize the comparison quotient, and transfer by strong coprimality.
Open mapping identifies a Fréchet target with the quotient by a closed synthesis kernel.
Residue cardinalities above one rational prime have commensurate logarithms.
The primary difference quotient has a finite rapid-sequence synthesis model.
Finite lattice synthesis is bijective for separating biorthogonal coordinates.
Count overlapping lattices with multiplicity, preserving the character coordinate.
Extend a norm-one character using a section of the idelic norm.
The inverse uniformizer class has norm equal to the residue cardinality.
Include the empty difference product, whose quotient and sequence source are both zero.
The moment basis identifies a nonempty commensurate difference quotient with rapid sequences.
Extra sequence coordinates may be discarded by a continuous surjection.
Selecting one of finitely many rapid sequences at each index preserves rapid decay.
Rapidly decreasing coefficients synthesize polynomially growing vectors continuously.
Use the unramified sequence model to realize the strong dual inside the prescribed ambient dual.
Coordinate projection has a continuous zero-extension right inverse, including empty products.
Pad the finite sequence model, transpose the retraction, and take the zero-kernel quotient.
Transposing a split surjection identifies its strong dual with a closed complemented subspace.
Open mapping upgrades bijective rapid-sequence synthesis to a topological linear equivalence.
Surjectivity of the induced quotient map decomposes each target vector as an image vector plus an element of the target denominator.
The section Mellin transform takes an unramified difference product to multiplication by its reciprocal Euler polynomial.
The Mellin character of a uniformizer gives the single-place Euler polynomial.
Translation of an isotypic function on a norm section multiplies its Mellin integral by the value of the Mellin character at the translating element.

The comparison denominator is an expanding difference-product range, whose quotient is separable, nuclear, and Fréchet. It repeats `strongCoprimalityPrimaryQuotient_decay`, which is declared after `strongCoprimality` and so is out of its reach.

Every exponentially decaying function of the isotype is the homogeneous theta function of a pole-free theta class, up to an element of the range of the difference product over the unramified places of `S`, each difference taken along the inverse class of `π v`.

Cardinal interpolation of summable values on the exponential lattice. The divided difference of the exponential is one at zero and vanishes at the other lattice points. Its imaginary translates are uniformly bounded on each vertical strip.
Removing the simple zeros of one reciprocal Euler factor gives an entire quotient. Imaginary periodicity of the factor preserves rapid decay on strips under this division.
The reciprocal Euler factor in exponential coordinates on the Mellin line.
At sufficiently large height the completed continuation is analytic. This is the two-pole argument used in `finiteHeckeL_continuation_isBigO_exp` in Appendix B.
Match the Mellin data of an arbitrary ambient function at all the zeros of one Euler factor by a pole-free theta transform, including the value at a canceled pole.

Interpolate the inverse of a function on a single Euler lattice. Dividing the samples by a power of `1 - z` makes their norms summable. The cardinal series then gives a bounded holomorphic interpolant on each strip, and restoring the power recovers the inverse.

A multiple of the regularized completed generator has polynomial growth on strips and polynomially bounded reciprocal at large height on the imaginary axis. Multiply by the epsilon factor and the reflected inverse gamma factor. The functional equation then identifies the result with the pole polynomial times the reflected finite L-function.
Successive single-place divisions keep the theta part divisible by the same entire generator. Each next division acts on the preceding quotient, including at shared zeros.

The entire interpolating multiplier preserves rapid decay on each vertical strip. Above the height threshold its polynomial growth is absorbed by a higher Schwartz weight. The remaining rectangle is compact.
A topological linear embedding with closed range into a Fréchet space, followed by a quotient map onto a Fréchet space, is open when every class of the target meets the range.

A pole-free homogeneous theta class lies in the principal-value denominator over `S` exactly when its homogeneous theta function lies in the range of the difference product over the unramified places of `S`, each difference taken along the inverse class of `π v`.

In the Mellin model, a Schwartz–Bergman function whose product with the reciprocal Euler product over unramified places is divisible by the regularized completed Hecke function is itself divisible by it: the zeros of the Euler product lie on the imaginary axis, where the completed function does not vanish.
The iterated difference of a function of the decay isotype is again a function of the decay isotype.

A Schwartz–Bergman function lies in the divisible subspace of an entire function exactly when it is that function times an entire function. It repeats the private `specDenom_mem_div` of `Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec4.lean`.

An entire function divides another one, with entire quotient, as soon as its vanishing order at every point is at most that of the other. The proof is the one of the private `archNuclearityMellin_range_entire_dvd` of `Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec4.lean`.
The reciprocal Euler product over a finite set of places is an entire function.
The Mellin character of a uniformizer gives the single-place Euler polynomial. It repeats `strongCoprimality_bezout_factor`, which is declared after `strongCoprimality`.

The Mellin model of the decay isotype takes an unramified difference product to multiplication by its reciprocal Euler polynomial. It repeats `strongCoprimality_bezout_difference`, which is declared after `strongCoprimality`.

After removing the two poles, the completed generator is nonzero in the closed left half-plane. It repeats the private `archNuclearityMellin_range_completed_ne_zero_left` of `Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec4.lean`.

The functional equation and the zero-free right boundary exclude completed zeros in the closed left half-plane. It repeats the private `archNuclearityMellin_range_completed_order_left` of `Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta/Sec4.lean`.
